and the derived comparison counts and error maxima.

## Laya larger GEMM tiles reduce a complete matrix boundary by 33% (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The persistent prototype now uses 32-by-64 GEMM output tiles, with the shared product
function still accepting attention's 16-by-32 tiles. The
[paired sitting](../results/laya/transformer_large_paired_desktop2_20261016.log)
measures a reduction from `12.06680703125` to `8.107720703125` ms for one M=512,
K=1024, N=1024 bf16 matrix product, including Python packet packing, mapped input copy,
input sync, submit/wait, output sync and detached output reconstruction. This is a
`32.809726034998%` reduction for that operator boundary, not a full-Laya speedup.
The existing hybrid still has CPU neural operations; independent command fixtures have
not yet been composed into an encoder block or checked against the pinned decisions.

### Implementation and geometry coverage

The larger tile uses the full output payload and twice as much activation and weight
payload per input packet. The persistent state grows to 2048 FP32 values; single-buffered
KV FIFOs replace the preceding double buffers so the linked SRAM placements still fit.
GEMM pads M to 128 rows, K to 64 features and N to 256 outputs with zero operands, checks
padded outputs are zero, and returns the original extent. Padding supports the action
head's 1028-wide input and small scorer/action outputs without a CPU matrix product.
It does not implement those heads' bias, activation or probability operations.

The [smoke](../results/laya/transformer_large_v1_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log) passes, followed
by the [expanded sitting](../results/laya/transformer_large_all_v1_suite_desktop2_20261016.log):
586 comparisons pass in one hardware context, with 293 instruction-layout changes and
a return to attention. There are 192 attention, 196 norm and 198 GEMM comparisons.
GEMM uses three seeds, random/zero/basis inputs and both output poisons for each shape:

| M | K | N | Purpose |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 512 | 1024 | 512 | Prior synthetic control geometry |
| 512 | 1024 | 3072 | QKV projection geometry |
| 512 | 1024 | 1024 | Projection geometry |
| 512 | 1024 | 5248 | Encoder MLP input geometry |
| 512 | 2624 | 1024 | Encoder MLP output geometry |
| 512 | 1024 | 4096 | Decision-head MLP input geometry |
| 512 | 4096 | 1024 | Decision-head MLP output geometry |
| 4 | 1024 | 1024 | Representative marker scorer geometry |
| 4 | 1024 | 1 | Representative marker logit geometry |
| 1 | 1028 | 256 | Action-head hidden geometry |
| 1 | 256 | 2 | Action-head output geometry |

Weights and activations are synthetic, not captured model tensors. These cases cover
the selected linear-operation geometries, not every possible marker count or the model's
accumulated numerical error. All previous attention and norm tolerances remain fixed;
norm residual bits remain exact. The [validation summary](../results/laya/transformer_large_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
records maximum absolute GEMM error `0.00014363322407007217`, attention error
`0.012427686459243192` and norm error `6.834568264224572e-06`. All input immutability,
poison independence, guards and unused output checks pass. The linked core occupies
13,168 bytes and passes the existing program, helper, stack and SRAM-span audits.
All initialization CDOs and core ELF hashes match across instruction layouts.
The numerical sitting is correctness-only; its durations do not qualify performance.

### Same-sitting paired performance

`kernels/laya_transformer/paired.py` compares the frozen `14c55c9` smaller-tile program
against the current larger-tile program. Registration hash:
`e3157193520919a49ebfa748d1dc6c84d06d92bddc342d43ddc0ee825f6664c3`.
The baseline checkout is clean, and both builds' source and artifact hashes are checked.
Both arms use the same stored bf16-valued operands and float64 reference. Each worker
checks both poisons before timing, releases its context and verifies idle while alive.
Workers are serial: the device never holds both comparison contexts together.

The preregistration fixes 16 ABBA blocks, eight timed samples after three warm-ups per
metric per worker. There are 256 timed samples per arm per metric. Reported means first
average each arm's two workers within a block, then average blocks. Approximate 95%
intervals use the 16 paired block differences and a normal approximation. Context
creation and source/artifact checking are excluded from both metrics.

| Scope | Smaller tile mean ms | Larger tile mean ms | Mean saving ms | Approximate 95% saving interval ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Prepared BO submit/wait | 5.62493046875 | 1.980509765625 | 3.644420703125 | 3.561169713604324 to 3.7276716926456763 |
| Packing through detached output | 12.06680703125 | 8.107720703125 | 3.959086328125 | 3.9069182346868208 to 4.011254421563179 |

Both preregistered reduction targets pass: at least 30% for dispatch and 20% for the
complete packet boundary, with a positive saving interval for the latter. Input BO bytes
fall from 8,454,144 to 4,227,072; output BO bytes from 8,519,680 to 2,129,920. This is a
comparison of the combined implementations: tile geometry, buffering, product addressing,
padding and packing all differ. It is not an isolated cycle-level tile-size ablation.
The wrapper reports a clear host load, no foreign NPU contention and timing eligible.
All 128 paired-worker correctness comparisons pass.

The paired win does not quantify the cost of single buffering or dynamic product
addressing for attention. No current whole-model latency can be inferred from this
matrix measurement. Host packing remains a substantial part of the boundary and must
be removed between model stages; rotary transforms, GeGLU, embedding/gather and the
remaining decision operations still need device implementations and composition.

Build all registered geometry cases with `program.py build --all-gemm`, then use
`program.py run --model ...` through the bounded correctness wrapper. For the comparison,
build a clean `14c55c9` control with `--gemm-n 1024`, register both directories using
`paired.py register --baseline ... --baseline-root ... --candidate ... --registration ...`,
and invoke `paired.py run --registration ...` through the timing-eligible research wrapper.
The [validation log](../results/laya/transformer_large_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
records 38 offline tests, the full legacy syntax/import and shell gates, default standalone
attention object identity, qualified comparison counts and the paired summary.

## Laya composed MLP: device handoffs work, strict chain gate fails (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

`kernels/laya_transformer/mlp.py` composes the two encoder MLP matrix products and
GeGLU in one dispatch: `[512,1024] -> [512,5248] -> [512,2624] -> [512,1024]`.
The first half of the first product passes through GELU and multiplies the second
half, matching the exported graph. Both products use bf16 operands and FP32
accumulation; GeGLU consumes FP32 and emits RNE bf16 in the next product's tiled
operand format. Static weights and activations occupy disjoint regions of one arena
BO. The same BO object supplies both kernel tensor arguments, preserving XRT
dependency tracking and the full allocation group ID. No scalar device address is used.

The instruction stream waits for producer DMA completion before consuming its region.
RTP selects the operation and K-block count after query acquisition; on-core counters
supply product reset/final flags without CPU rewriting of an intermediate header.
Each GeGLU worker consumes the four multicast value packets and selects its own row
packet. The second product gathers device-packed blocks directly. Its M groups use
separate DMA transfers and completion waits to fit the Shim dimension limits.
There are zero inter-stage host reads, writes or syncs: all three phases execute
inside one kernel call. They still traverse DDR. Inputs and weights are initialized
before dispatch, and CPU reference work reads results only after the complete chain.

### Retained failures

The [build/validation record](../results/laya/mlp_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
records the compile-only attempts; the [ELF/disassembly re-audit](../results/laya/mlp_build_reaudit_desktop2_20261016.log)
recomputes their sizes and conservative stack bounds from the retained artifacts.
A row-constant dispatcher produced cores up to
16,736 bytes and failed CDO loading; the selector now comes from RTP. Outlining GELU
reduces its recorded frames, and the prototype reserves a larger stack while keeping
the conservative sum-of-frames audit. A full-shape transfer with four active dimensions
and a long inner packet was rejected before execution; separate M-group transfers fix
that representation. These were build failures, not NPU timing measurements.

The [first smoke](../results/laya/mlp_v4_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log) stops before context
creation because SciPy is absent. The runner now uses Python's `math.erf` for the
qualification oracle. [Negative-input GeGLU](../results/laya/mlp_v5_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
then fails while both linear checks pass. The [diagnostic](../results/laya/mlp_v6_diagnostic_desktop2_20261016.log)
shows corrupted negative-gate results. Object disassembly shows `abs(float-vector)`
lowering to integer `vabs_gtz.s32`. Explicit IEEE sign-bit clearing and floating
subtraction for negation pass the [small-chain smoke](../results/laya/mlp_v7_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log).
The two source changes were applied together; this is not an isolated negation ablation.

### Full-size result remains FAIL

The [first full-size run](../results/laya/mlp_full_v9_suite_desktop2_20261016.log) passes
both linear checks and GeGLU but fails the strict final-output pointwise gate. The
[collected suite](../results/laya/mlp_full_v10_collected_desktop2_20261016.log) keeps the
same tolerances, visits every case, then exits with failure. It makes 74 comparisons:
three seeds times random/zero/basis patterns times two initial poisons, plus all 28
actual encoder weight pairs with one synthetic activation fixture and two poisons.
The graph and each selected original weight tensor are hashed. These are not captured
model activations or complete model predictions.

| Check | Passing comparisons | Maximum absolute error | Maximum relative L2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First matrix product | 74 / 74 | 0.00001006200909614563 | 0.00000024801637034534055 |
| GeGLU including bf16 output conversion | 74 / 74 | 0.41497044447720555 | 0.001672879531625274 |
| Second matrix product against device-GeGLU operands | 74 / 74 | 0.001150188036262989 | 0.00000081831224464871 |
| Complete chain against independent reference | 12 of 74 (DERIVED from logged verdicts) | 0.03418919383227603 | 0.00006962958481509391 |

Each linear check requires `abs <= 0.0002 + 0.0002*abs(ref)` and relative L2 at most
`0.00001`. GeGLU, including its intentional bf16 rounding, requires
`abs <= 0.000002 + 0.0078125*abs(ref)` and relative L2 at most `0.004`.
The complete-chain check requires `abs <= 0.0002 + 0.002*abs(ref)` and relative L2
at most `0.002`. Its relative L2 passes, but 62 comparisons fail pointwise. Small
arithmetic differences crossing bf16 rounding boundaries are a plausible explanation;
their contribution was not isolated from nonlinear approximation error in that sitting
(the follow-up below now decomposes it).
The gates are not loosened, and this is not a qualified full-size MLP accuracy result.

All guards, untouched arena regions, input/weight immutability, padded rows/columns,
written payloads and poison-independence checks pass. One context serves the suite
and releases idle while the process is alive. The arena occupies 37,395,840 bytes.
Every linked core is 15,488 bytes; helper, physical SRAM span and conservative stack
audits pass with a 4,608-byte stack reservation. The program also links attention/norm,
but their transitions through this new RTP dispatcher have not been qualified.

The [validation log](../results/laya/mlp_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) records the
full legacy syntax/import/shell checks and 41 offline tests. New independent tests
cover arena separation, every full-shape gate/value feature address and every byte
of the second product's activation gather, including padded token rows.
All hardware runs here are correctness-only. Their logged dispatch durations do not
establish a speedup or complete-Laya latency. At this milestone rotary transforms,
attention operand conversion, embedding/gather, residual/norm composition and the
decision tail remained required. The next result composes rotary and attention;
complete-model pinned decision accuracy and same-sitting timing remain open.

### MLP numerical isolation: both upstream rounding and nonlinear error contribute

The [post-dispatch diagnostic sitting](../results/laya/mlp_isolation_v11_desktop2_20261016.log)
retains the same core ELF hashes and strict gate failures. It evaluates an exact
nonlinear reference twice: once on the independent first-product reference and once
on the device's actual first-product output. Both are rounded to bf16. Their difference
isolates upstream arithmetic crossing operand-rounding boundaries. Comparing the latter
with actual device GeGLU isolates nonlinear/conversion differences. Multiplying each
difference by the second weight matrix, then adding that product's accumulation
residual, reconstructs the final-output error. No reference tensor feeds the device.

The [derived summary](../results/laya/rotary_isolation_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
covers 37 distinct cases and 74 poison comparisons. Upstream arithmetic changes 12,305
rounded activation elements; nonlinear/conversion differences change another 11,816
transitions, across distinct cases. These are transition counts, not disjoint sets of
positions. The first-product contribution has larger L2 than the nonlinear contribution
in 31 cases. Maximum output contributions are `0.034179835580289364` from upstream
rounding, `0.017221901565775632` from nonlinear/conversion differences and
`0.001150188036262989` from final-product accumulation. The decomposition closes to
`2.4868995751603507e-14`. This isolates error contributions under these fixtures; it
does not establish a model decision impact or excuse the retained pointwise failure.

## Laya projection through RoPE and attention: device-owned intermediates pass (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

`kernels/laya_transformer/rotary.py` composes `[512,1024]` input, a `[1024,3072]` QKV
projection, rotary Q/K, device packet formatting and attention. All phases run in one
kernel call on one hardware context, using a shared arena and completion waits.
There are zero host reads, writes or syncs between phases. Intermediate tensors still
travel through DDR. CPU oracles supply no device activation.

Before inference, the builder constant-folds the exported model's rotary ancestors
for fixed sequence positions, preserving the actual global/local frequency constants.
It hashes the resulting FP32 coefficient packets. There is no per-call host rotary
calculation. Q/K rotate in FP32 and convert to bf16 with explicit RNE. Separate
query-half commands emit the existing attention headers and 4-by-8 query tiles. Keys
transpose to 8-by-4 tiles; another device command merges K with tiled V and the key
index ramp. Query rows with finite-mask uniform semantics are zeroed on the device.

### Code budget and transfer representation

The combined image including GeGLU occupies 18,064 bytes/core and is rejected before
hardware execution. The [validation record](../results/laya/rotary_isolation_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
reads the retained ELF sizes. The attention image therefore omits GeGLU and occupies
15,408 bytes/core, retaining GEMM and norm code. The MLP image is separate. Serial
cross-image BO handoff and its scheduling cost have not been measured; neither chain
establishes complete-model execution in one image.

The compiler also rejects the first gapped KV transfer's oversized inner dimension.
Splitting packets into vector-word chunks fits the Shim dimensions. The runtime writes
only changed RTP values and waits before reusing descriptor slots. Every core ELF and
all initialization CDO payloads match across the eight instruction layouts. Conservative
stack bound is 4,064 bytes within the 4,608-byte reservation; unresolved-helper and
physical SRAM-span checks pass. The arena occupies 27,756,032 bytes.

### Qualification and scope

The [first smoke](../results/laya/rotary_v3_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log) passes both initial
poisons for global/full-valid attention. The [first expanded suite](../results/laya/rotary_v4_all_suite_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes but its per-comparison layout label is overwritten by a region-loop variable.
Keep that reporting failure; use the [repeated, correctly labelled suite](../results/laya/rotary_v5_all_model_suite_desktop2_20261016.log)
for per-layout coverage. It passes 160 comparisons in one context, 20 for each of
global/local with valid-key counts 512, 193, 1 and 0. There are three seeds times
random/zero/basis patterns times two poisons for every layout, plus the first encoder's
actual QKV weights on one synthetic activation fixture, again with both poisons for
every layout. The latter accounts for 16 comparisons, not every layer's weights.
The selected tensor is `val_164`, SHA256
`8cda894d0d44b0bd583b51f32de7b939d66817136c39a8a2550f8ba2087d7887`.

Each stage and the composed attention output use the existing attention tolerance:
`abs <= 0.01 + 0.02*abs(ref)` and relative L2 at most `0.02`. Maximum composed absolute
error is `0.006138631457476895`; maximum composed relative L2 is
`0.0035116222030673453`. A separate attention-core check uses actual device-prepared
Q/K/V after completion to distinguish attention error from preparation error. Query
metadata, both output poisons, input/weight/coefficient immutability, arena gaps, output
guards, written payloads and key ramps pass. The context releases idle while the process
is alive, with no foreign contention observed.

The [validation log](../results/laya/rotary_isolation_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
records the full legacy syntax/import/shell gates and 46 offline tests. New independent
checks cover every output DMA word exactly once, arena separation, all Q/K/V source-tile
addresses and all transferred query/key/value data words.

All hardware runs here are correctness-only: their durations establish no latency win.
Inputs are synthetic, including when the first actual projection weights are used.
At this milestone the output projection, residual/norm composition, embedding/gather,
MLP connection and decision tail remained required. The next result extends the chain
through residual/norm. Complete Laya inference, pinned decision accuracy and same-sitting
whole-model performance remain unverified.

## Laya attention through residual and norm: MLP input prepared on device (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The attention image now runs QKV projection, RoPE, attention, its output projection,
FP32 residual addition, LayerNorm and conversion of normalized output to the next
GEMM's bf16 tile format. All phases execute in one kernel call with one context and
shared arena. Host reads, writes and syncs occur only outside the complete chain.
This qualifies the attention sublayer and MLP-input preparation, not a complete encoder
block or model. The separate MLP image has not consumed this buffer in a chained run.

### Layout connects the operators without a host gather

A device command joins pairs of attention outputs into 32-by-64 bf16 operand tiles,
checking exact RNE conversion. The output projection consumes those device-owned
tiles. Its special finish stores each token's feature tile as 64 FP32 values plus a
guard. Shim DMA scatters these tiles directly into the norm input, preserving the
original residual vector. Residuals retain their original FP32 bits; only GEMM inputs
round to bf16. Random fixtures include non-bf16 residual bits to exercise that split.

The norm input uses 16 guarded feature tiles, then the original residual, then a tail
guard. Unaligned vector loads skip the feature guards. The integer FP32 RNE residual
adder and all existing norm tolerances remain in force. Norm output places normalized
Y first, then a guard, residual sum R, and a tail guard. This layout lets a later
projection overwrite the X tile region while retaining R for its next residual add;
that later MLP connection remains untested.

Another device command gathers normalized rows and emits the same bf16 GEMM operand
tiles, again checking exact RNE bits. It currently replays full norm packets per
feature tile, so traffic optimization remains open. The norm sets the arithmetic
rounding mode; the existing fence restores attention's required mode. The builder
verifies the emitted reset, and repeated full-chain dispatches exercise norm followed
by later attention commands.

These layouts compile only with `TRANSFORMER_NORM_TILED`. The [validation log](../results/laya/attention_norm_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
compiles the default norm and dispatch objects without that flag and verifies both
are byte-identical to the preceding default program. The graph engine's accepted
model vocabulary is unchanged.

### Qualification and limits

The [output-projection smoke](../results/laya/output_projection_v1_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes before norm integration. The [first norm smoke](../results/laya/attention_norm_v1_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes with the earlier diagnostic output layout. The [next smoke](../results/laya/attention_norm_v2_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes with the final residual-preserving layout and MLP-input conversion. These are
historical ABI steps; the [expanded suite](../results/laya/attention_norm_v3_all_suite_desktop2_20261016.log)
backs the final result.

All 160 comparisons pass: 20 for each global/local layout with valid-key counts 512,
193, 1 and 0. Three seeds, random/zero/basis inputs and two poisons account for 144;
the first encoder's actual QKV/output weights and MLP-norm affine set on one synthetic
activation fixture account for 16. Selected tensors and hashes are in the log.
All intermediate guards, untouched regions, original residual bits, input/weight
immutability, output writes and poison independence pass.

The residual sum matches CPU FP32 RNE bits exactly. Attention-to-GEMM and norm-to-GEMM
conversions also match their bf16 RNE oracles exactly. Direct norm checks retain
`abs <= 0.0002 + 0.0002*abs(ref)` and relative L2 at most `0.0002`. Their maximum
absolute error is `1.808657471258357e-05`, maximum relative L2
`1.5479263296809562e-07`. Composed output-projection and norm checks retain the
attention gate `abs <= 0.01 + 0.02*abs(ref)`, relative L2 at most `0.02`.
Maximum composed norm error is `0.009743085569756005`, relative L2
`0.0007796955581473922`. Direct operator checks use actual device intermediates only
after the entire chain finishes; no oracle result supplies a neural input.

Every linked core occupies 16,192 bytes. Conservative stack bound is 4,160 bytes
within the 4,608-byte reservation, with helper and physical SRAM audits passing.
Core and initialization hashes match across all eight instruction layouts. The arena
occupies 42,657,728 bytes. One context serves all comparisons and releases idle while
the process is alive; no foreign contention is observed. All hardware runs here are
correctness-only, so their durations establish no speedup or model latency.
The [validation](../results/laya/attention_norm_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) records
49 offline tests plus the full legacy syntax/import/shell gates. Independent DMA tests
cover every output word, preservation of residual regions and all conversion/gather
addresses. MLP connection, embeddings, remaining layers, decision head, pinned accuracy
and same-sitting complete-model performance remain open. The MLP's earlier strict
pointwise failure is unchanged by this attention result.

### Frozen evaluation inputs restored, no new accuracy result

The [item restoration](../results/laya/eval_items_restore_desktop2_20261016.log) rebuilds
the missing local evaluation file from the dataset revisions recorded in the original
preparation log. All per-task hashes and the complete file hash match the existing
[preregistration](../results/laya/laya_accuracy_prereg_desktop2_20260926.json): 2,400 labelled
items plus three fixture questions, SHA256
`138b8a76ce66af5e838e2558832be3f0d33b8740c326ba35616185d079f33f59`.
The [reference restoration](../results/laya/eval_reference_restore_desktop2_20261016.log)

Its hash matches the preregistration, as do the current original model and external

## Laya complete encoder-block handoff: operators pass, composition fails (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [collected smoke](../results/laya/block_v5_collected_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
connects attention, output projection, residual/norm, Wi, GeGLU, Wo and the following
residual/norm across two resident native programs. Both dispatches share one arena BO;
all input/weight uploads precede the first dispatch, and the first activation read follows
the second completion. There are no interstage host reads, writes or syncs. Preserve the
full allocation group ID and check compatible bank bits for both kernel arguments.

The MLP consumes the attention program's packed normalized output directly. Its Wo
scatters into the now-dead normalized-Y region while preserving the FP32 residual
alongside it. The next norm consumes that pair. This qualifies a device handoff on
synthetic activations, not inference on a real token sequence or the complete model.

Four comparisons cover random synthetic weights and the first actual encoder block's
weights, each with two initial buffer poisons. Every per-operator gate passes; direct
residual additions are bit-exact and final outputs agree across poisons. The independent
composed reference still fails for both synthetic-weight comparisons: normalized output
has 14 bad pointwise elements, maximum absolute error 0.017136947254509205 and relative
L2 0.0020829767533175124; the carried residual has 1,589 bad pointwise elements. Both
actual-weight comparisons pass this composed gate on their synthetic activation input.
The stricter retained MLP comparison fails all four comparisons. No tolerances changed,
and the runner exits nonzero after collecting those failures. Small relative L2 does not
turn a failed pointwise gate into a pass.

The [earlier attempt](../results/laya/block_v3_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log) reaches both
dispatches and detects the same numerical failure, then crashes during PyXRT teardown.
Release instruction BOs and kernels before their contexts, then xclbins and device.
The [next attempt](../results/laya/block_v4_collected_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log) proves
clean teardown but exposes a harness guard error: the untouched norm-input tail should
retain its initial fill, rather than the output poison. The collected smoke fixes that
expectation and reports device idle while its process is alive. Both failed logs remain.

The [validation record](../results/laya/block_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes
54 offline tests plus the full legacy syntax/import/shell gate. Independent tests cover
all output bytes, residual preservation and every transferred operand byte. Linked
programs occupy 16,192 bytes per attention core and 15,152 per MLP core; stack, helper
and SRAM audits pass. The shared arena occupies 80,078,208 bytes. These are checks-only
runs: dispatch durations in their logs are not eligible speed evidence. Numerical
composition, remaining layers, embeddings, head, frozen decision accuracy and complete
model performance remain open.

### Experimental FP32 exponential and two-part probabilities

The [first FP32-table block smoke](../results/laya/block_exp_v2_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
regresses composition. Isolation exposes an implementation error rather than an accuracy
tradeoff: the [initial isolated runner](../results/laya/exp_isolation_v1_desktop2_20261016.log)
fails an import before opening hardware; the [wide-range probe](../results/laya/exp_isolation_v2_desktop2_20261016.log)
and [equal-input lanes](../results/laya/exp_isolation_v3_lanes_desktop2_20261016.log)
show alternating lookup errors. The [raw-index diagnostic](../results/laya/exp_isolation_v4_raw_layout_desktop2_20261016.log)
measures physical table positions. FP32 lookup banks require duplicated groups of four
entries, `[v0,v1,v2,v3,v0,v1,v2,v3]`, rather than adjacent duplicates. Its raw-index
outputs are diagnostic values, not exponential accuracy measurements.

The [corrected-layout probe](../results/laya/exp_isolation_v5_correct_layout_desktop2_20261016.log)
still fails its relative-error gate near the small end of the range. Replace floating
power-of-two multiplication with an exact FP32 exponent-bit adjustment on the clamped
normal domain. The [next probe](../results/laya/exp_isolation_v6_exponent_bits_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes. The [source-bound expanded probe](../results/laya/exp_qualified_v1_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes 12 comparisons: a range sweep over `[-80,0]`, zero on every lane, all table
entries on every physical lookup lane, and two buffer poisons. Maximum relative error
is 5.652042801634955e-06 against the unchanged 0.00002 isolated gate; guards and poison
independence pass. This is sampled operator coverage, not a proof over every FP32 input.

The [bank-layout block smoke](../results/laya/block_exp_v3_bank_layout_desktop2_20261016.log)
and [exponent-bit block smoke](../results/laya/block_exp_v4_exponent_bits_desktop2_20261016.log)
reduce error but retain composition failures. The next candidate also stores high and
low bf16 probability parts and accumulates both products with V, using the shared GEMM
body with a shorter K loop. It compacts low parts into already-consumed score storage,
retains FP32 denominator sums and requires no additional scratch arena. Its
[smoke](../results/laya/block_probs_v1_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log) passes normalized
output checks but retains synthetic residual and strict MLP failures.

The [global-mask suite](../results/laya/block_probs_v1_global_suite_desktop2_20261016.log)
collects 20 comparisons: three synthetic seeds with random, zero and basis patterns,
plus the first actual encoder block's weights on synthetic activations, each with two
poisons. Every direct operator gate and every normalized block-output gate passes.
Composed residual and retained strict MLP gates each fail 12 comparisons; the runner
correctly exits nonzero. For the initial synthetic random case, normalized relative L2
falls from 0.0020829767533175124 to 0.001097905596911174 and its bad pointwise count
falls from 14 to zero. Residual bad elements fall from 1,589 to 72. This is improved
numerical behavior, not a fully passing block. Both actual-weight smoke comparisons
pass all retained gates, but their input is still synthetic.

The [validation](../results/laya/block_precision_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes 55 offline tests and the full legacy syntax/import/shell checks. Default attention
and GEMM objects remain byte-identical. The candidate attention image occupies 15,600
bytes per core, conservative stack bound 4,768 bytes within a 4,864-byte reservation;
MLP remains 15,152 bytes with bound 4,448 within 4,608. SRAM/helper audits pass. These
paths are opt-in through `--precise-exp --precise-probs`; existing default programs keep
their arithmetic. All runs are checks-only. Other mask layouts, real token inputs,
remaining layers, embeddings/head, frozen decisions and eligible end-to-end timing are
still unverified for this candidate.

### Dynamic mask instructions without recompiling the core image

The [dynamic smoke](../results/laya/block_dynamic_v1_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
derives the valid/local RTP addresses from each core's own audited control allocation.
It patches only explicit WRITE value fields; no instruction word is selected by its
numeric value. Base controls must have one initial write per core/field, and changed
framing, missing cores, duplicate writes or unexpected register encodings are refused.

Before hardware execution, the patcher compares all other operation bytes and the
valid/local state consumed by query-header commands against eight independently
compiled reference streams. It also checks framing and control slots for every valid
length from zero through 512, in both global and local modes: 1,026 offline variants.
This does not establish hardware coverage for every length. The executable cores and
initialization image remain the source-bound precise-probability block image; only
instruction controls differ.

On Desktop 2, 32 smoke comparisons cover global/local masks at valid lengths 512, 193,
one and zero, synthetic random weights and the first actual block weights on synthetic
activations, and both buffer poisons. All direct operator checks pass and cleanup
reports idle while alive. Two normalized-output, 14 residual-composition and 24 retained
strict MLP comparisons fail. These numerical failures remain nonzero exits, not a
qualification of complete-block accuracy. The [validation](../results/laya/block_dynamic_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes 66 offline tests and the full legacy syntax/import/shell checks. The new tests
exercise relocated register allocations, wrong live values despite otherwise identical
operations, corrupt framing, missing cores and already-patched bases. No eligible timing
was collected. Arbitrary lengths on silicon and repeated encoder layers remain open.

## Laya encoder trunk: 28-layer execution, composed accuracy fails (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [two-layer smoke](../results/laya/chain_v3_two_layers_smoke_desktop2_20261016.log)
connects successive attention/MLP blocks without a host activation handoff. Before the
next QKV projection, the attention program packs the preceding MLP norm output on
device. Its output projection then overwrites that buffer's dead Y region while
preserving the FP32 residual alongside it. The old packed-input region can be reused
after QKV has consumed it. No new activation copy operator is required.

The second QKV output passes a direct comparison against the separately observed
first-prefix output. That observation supplies an oracle only; it is never fed back
to the device. Both prefixes start from the same fresh initial buffer. All inputs,
constants and instructions are uploaded before the prefix's first dispatch, and its
first host activation read follows its final completion. Shared input, constant banks
and arena borders remain unchanged; output guards and poison independence pass.

The [first complete-trunk run](../results/laya/chain_v4_28_layers_desktop2_20261016.log)
executes all 28 encoder layers, using the exported graph's actual weights and rotary
dependencies: ten global and 18 local attention layers. Constant banks are resident in
one shared arena; decoded DDR_PATCH fields relocate their reads by bank and preserve
activation/output addresses. The repeated instruction stream has identical executable
cores and initialization payloads to the initial attention stream, allowing both in
one attention context. The MLP uses a second context. Each complete trunk executes
56 serialized dispatches with zero interstage host reads, writes or syncs.

This is a boundary experiment, not complete Laya inference. It supplies one synthetic
array as both the initial normalized-input operand and initial residual. It does not
perform token embedding or embedding normalization, use a real token sequence, or run
the type embedding, head, scorer or action/decision tail. Its independent CPU reference
uses rounded bf16 GEMM operands and the existing attention/nonlinear/norm oracles;
it is not the frozen full-model FP32 logits comparison.

Runs inspect prefixes of one, two and 28 layers, each with two initial buffer poisons.
The [second sequence length](../results/laya/chain_v4_28_layers_valid512_desktop2_20261016.log)
also completes the trunk. Both runs pass direct final projection/norm checks, the
two-layer QKV handoff check, exact final residual addition, guards and unchanged-bank
checks. Full-trunk composition fails at both lengths:

| Valid keys | Normalized-output relative L2 | Bad normalized elements | Residual relative L2 | Bad residual elements |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 193 | 0.05404254057113863 | 54,327 | 0.0428159162402153 | 224,951 |
| 512 | 0.038391644857506416 | 60,280 | 0.04756646230816841 | 207,801 |

Keep those failures. The initial chain runner did not report the earlier strict MLP
gate, so its absence must not be read as a pass. The [retained-gate repeat](../results/laya/chain_v5_28_retained_gates_desktop2_20261016.log)
adds direct Wi/GeGLU checks and that unchanged strict MLP comparison. At valid length
193, all direct operator and handoff checks pass; normalized composition fails both
28-layer comparisons, residual composition fails both two- and 28-layer comparisons,
and strict MLP also fails both two- and 28-layer comparisons. Numerical outputs match
the earlier length-193 run. The process exits nonzero and releases idle while alive.
No tolerance, frozen item/reference file or complete-model decision criterion changed.

The [validation record](../results/laya/chain_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes
70 offline tests and the legacy syntax/import/shell gates. Tests independently cover
every repeated-stream output word, preservation of residual/constant regions, all QKV
feature/core addresses, all constant-bank bounds and constant-only instruction edits.
Default compiled cores, initialization payloads and instruction bytes remain identical
after factoring the existing norm packer. Repeated attention remains 15,600 bytes per
core, MLP 15,152, with the previous stack/SRAM/helper audits retained. The shared
28-layer arena occupies 754,752,448 bytes. CPU verification no longer retains the
materialized original FP32 model graph after extracting its independent constants.

All measurements here are checks-only. Wrapper durations include CPU oracles, transfers
and extensive buffer verification; they establish neither trunk inference latency nor
end-to-end speed. Accuracy accumulation remains unresolved. Embedding/head coverage,
real-input frozen decision evaluation and eligible complete-model performance remain open.

## Laya token embeddings through the encoder: real inputs, accuracy still fails (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

**Superseded integration assumption:** these runs seed the first encoder residual from
raw embedding E. The exported graph instead adds normalized embedding Y. Operator
checks remain evidence for the tested inputs, but this is not the original model's
residual wiring. See the [correction and full-output fixture](#laya-full-device-outputs-fixture-qualification-and-first-residual-correction-2026-10-16-desktop-2).

The embedding stage keeps the original FP32 embedding table and norm affine in a
resident input BO. The host schedules Shim DMA addresses from token IDs; it performs
no floating embedding gather to supply device activations. NPU code copies each selected
row into the guarded norm packet and normalizes it on device. Integer address scheduling
is host work and is part of the method. CPU gathers and mask extraction in this harness
are independent references, never activation or mask inputs to the device.

The copy preserves the embedding as the following encoder residual. A separate stem-norm
command restores its original bits after normalization, including signed zero; the
ordinary MLP residual-add/norm command keeps its previous semantics. Reads at the last
vocabulary row use explicit padding after the table. Four distinct query descriptors
are reused only after their group completes. Token IDs, packet bounds and destination
rows are checked before instruction preparation.

The [first probe](../results/laya/stem_v2_probe_desktop2_20261016.log) and
[diagnostic repeat](../results/laya/stem_v2_diagnostic_desktop2_20261016.log) fail output
guards. The new commands entered the norm family but still satisfied the old generic
GEMM-finish guard, emitting an extra packet. Extend the complement guard to the complete
norm family. The [corrected probe](../results/laya/stem_v3_probe_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes eight comparisons across edge IDs, reversed order, repeated final-row IDs and
fixture tokens, with two buffer poisons. The [full-length suite](../results/laya/stem_v4_full_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes six comparisons over 512-token fixture, sequential and repeated-ID cases. Norm
maximum absolute error is 1.427653117502814e-06, with the original norm tolerances
unchanged; selected residual bits, guards, poison independence and the entire resident
constant BO pass their checks.

The [first integrated attempt](../results/laya/embedded_v1_fixture_encoder_desktop2_20261016.log)
fails a fixture-key variable collision before opening a device context. The
[fixture run](../results/laya/embedded_v2_fixture_encoder_desktop2_20261016.log) and
[first labelled-item run](../results/laya/embedded_v3_labelled_encoder_desktop2_20261016.log)
then execute the embedding/norm stage directly into the complete encoder. The stem's
output uses the existing residual/Y arena slot. The initial QKV reads its on-device
packed Y; unused host-input activation slots remain poisoned. Stem output addresses
and layer-zero constant reads are relocated through decoded DDR_PATCH fields.

The expanded MLP image supports the original MLP commands as well as the stem. Its
physical FIFO/control layout and initialization connectivity match the prior MLP image,
so two serialized contexts serve the whole path. Every embedding-plus-encoder run uses
57 dispatches with zero interstage host activation reads, writes or syncs. Constants,
arena borders and unused original input/residual regions remain unchanged. Independent
first- and second-QKV checks use separately observed prefix outputs only as oracles.

Input provenance is checked against the frozen item file and its existing hash. Item
zero is the fixture with 91 valid tokens; item three is the first labelled AG News item
with 83 valid tokens. The same padding token and original token IDs are used. Each run
inspects stem-only and one-, two- and 28-layer prefixes under both poisons. Direct stem,
Wi, GeGLU, Wo, final norm/residual-bit and QKV handoff checks pass. Composed accuracy
still fails against the independent quantized-product reference:

| Item | Valid keys | Full-encoder normalized relative L2 | Bad normalized elements | Residual relative L2 | Bad residual elements |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fixture, index 0 | 91 | 0.020210834331721016 | 31,777 | 0.03781760111451149 | 165,220 |
| AG News, index 3 | 83 | 0.032432899840085 | 55,843 | 0.028616247698664665 | 217,729 |

For each item, both full-encoder normalized comparisons fail; residual composition and
the retained strict MLP comparison fail all six non-stem comparisons. These failures
remain nonzero exits with unchanged thresholds. They are encoder comparisons, not
classification accuracy measurements or the frozen full-model logits/decision evaluation.
The type embedding, two head layers, scorer and action/decision tail remain absent.

The [validation](../results/laya/stem_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes 80 offline
tests and the full legacy syntax/import/shell gates. New tests cover every stem output
word, descriptor reuse, interleaved token-address ordering, constant-only and output-only
instruction edits, bad token vectors and the extra-output regression. The arbitrary-length
mask oracle matches all eight existing reference layouts; device masks still come from
RTP controls. Factoring the original chain initializer preserves its complete buffer
bytes. The expanded MLP/stem image occupies 16,016 bytes per core, conservative stack
bound 4,480 within 4,608; SRAM/helper audits pass. All device runs release idle while
their processes remain alive. All runs are checks-only and include CPU reference work
and extensive verification, so their wrapper durations establish no inference latency
or speedup. Complete-model coverage, frozen decisions and eligible performance remain open.

## Laya first head prelude: device type embedding, norm and biased QKV (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

These runs inherit the raw-embedding initial-residual error above. See the
[corrected model integration](#laya-full-device-outputs-fixture-qualification-and-first-residual-correction-2026-10-16-desktop-2);
their direct operator comparisons do not validate that earlier graph assumption.

The [fixture run](../results/laya/head_pre_v2_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log) and
[first labelled-item run](../results/laya/head_pre_v3_labelled_desktop2_20261016.log)
extend real-token inference through the first head's QKV projection. After the entire
encoder, device code combines its normalized output with the resident type embedding,
applies the head's learned LayerNorm gamma and beta, packs the result, computes QKV and
adds its original FP32 bias. The host selects constant-table DMA addresses from qtype;
it supplies no floating activation for this handoff. All constants and instructions are
resident before the first dispatch. Each complete prelude run uses 58 serial dispatches,
two resident contexts and zero interstage host activation reads, writes or syncs.

The new vector/MLP image removes its unreachable attention branch; the attention image
continues to execute attention. Linked executable code occupies 14,624 bytes per core.
The conservative stack bound is 5,184 bytes within a 5,376-byte reservation. Physical
output buffers move with the larger stack. Compatibility therefore uses independently
compiled, byte-identical original stem and encoder instruction streams, unchanged RTP
addresses, and identical executable/initialization payloads across the **new** stem,
encoder and head layouts. It does not claim old and new physical buffer allocations
match. The new image is loaded into its own fresh context. All linked cores pass the
SRAM, helper and stack audits in the [validation record](../results/laya/vector_head_validation_desktop2_20261016.log).

The [initial operator suite](../results/laya/vector_v2_operators_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes 42 comparisons. Its GELU tolerance is superseded by the
[strict repeat](../results/laya/vector_v3_strict_operators_desktop2_20261016.log), which
also passes 42: seven commands, three seeds and two buffer poisons. Bias/ReLU packing,
plain and tiled biased FP32 outputs, type-seed formatting, residual sum and norm packing
match the independent expected bits. GELU compares its BF16 output with independently
rounded erf-GELU using absolute 0.000002, relative 0.0078125 and relative-L2 0.004 gates;
it is not bit-exact. Guards, unowned output words, read-only inputs and poison independence
pass. These synthetic inputs do not establish complete head accuracy.

Both integrated inputs retain their frozen token IDs, padding and qtype zero. Prefixes
stop after the stem, encoder layers one, two and 28, and the new head prelude, each with
both poisons. The separate encoder-prefix observation is an oracle only; it never feeds
the later device run. Type-seed X matches those encoder output bits, the selected type
row matches exactly, head norm retains exact residual-add bits, packed head input matches
BF16 rounding, and the biased QKV passes the original direct linear tolerances. Maximum
direct norm absolute errors are 2.3956211592235377e-06 (fixture) and
3.1703985552411496e-06 (labelled item); maximum biased-QKV absolute error is
1.71661376953125e-05 on both.

**Composition still fails.** The original encoder and strict MLP failures remain
explicit nonzero exits. The head norm also fails the composed pointwise comparison
against the independent encoder reference:

| Input | Head normalized relative L2 | Bad normalized elements | Head residual relative L2 | Bad residual elements |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fixture, valid keys 91 | 0.016681330971853172 | 7,841 | 0.015403006225824356 | 21,316 |
| AG News, valid keys 83 | 0.02479055972651689 | 20,778 | 0.023254385218024254 | 40,023 |

The [validation](../results/laya/vector_head_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes
90 offline tests and the full legacy syntax/import/shell gates. New tests cover every
head output word, in-place projection ownership, constant-only type address patches,
invalid types, activation packing and dispatch-family output suppression. Both device
processes release idle while still alive; no foreign device owner is observed. All
runs are checks-only and their durations include CPU references and extensive checking.
The remaining two head attention/MLP blocks, scorer and action tail still prevent
complete model outputs. Frozen decision accuracy and eligible whole-model speed remain
unmeasured; this checkpoint establishes neither a speedup nor complete-model correctness.

## Laya both head blocks: device attention and ReLU MLPs, scorer still absent (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

These runs also inherit the initial raw-embedding residual error. Their measured direct
checks stand, while the [later graph correction](#laya-full-device-outputs-fixture-qualification-and-first-residual-correction-2026-10-16-desktop-2)
supersedes their integration with the original model.

The [first head-attention run](../results/laya/head_attention_v3_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log)
consumes the resident biased QKV without recomputing it. Identity cosine/sine packets
reuse the qualified conversion instructions, and the resulting unrotated Q/K/V match
the rounded biased projection bits exactly. The head uses global valid-key attention,
then packs its output for the following matrix product. Existing attention tolerances
remain unchanged. Maximum direct attention absolute error is 5.5699496225747325e-05,
relative L2 4.2171160078342885e-06. Query headers, key ramps, guards and packed output
pass their checks. The head's exported negative-infinity mask and the encoder's finite
mask select the same keys for nonempty input; empty head masks are explicitly refused.
This is not a qualification of their differing all-masked semantics.

The [first head post stage](../results/laya/head_post_v1_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log)
adds its output projection and FP32 bias, residual/norm2, a biased ReLU MLP and the
following head's norm1. Output weights are transposed according to the exported Gemm;
the MLP retains its original ReLU and biases. A separate activation bank accommodates
the wider ReLU result. Biased projection scatter overwrites only X, preserving R until
the next residual operation. All direct linear, bias, ReLU and final norm checks pass.
The packed norm2 comparison permits its BF16 rounding error; it does not claim a retained
FP32 norm2 observation after the buffer is reused. Composition still fails: the following
head's normalized input has relative L2 0.0023444427162116494 with 1,593 pointwise failures,
and residual relative L2 0.00790910143405199 with 19,684 failures.

The second head is then connected on the
[fixture](../results/laya/head_second_v1_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log) and
[first labelled AG News item](../results/laya/head_second_v2_labelled_desktop2_20261016.log).
Its QKV reads the previous on-device norm, reuses the same attention program and follows
with its own learned output projection, norm2 and biased ReLU MLP. The final operation
is the graph's raw residual sum, with no added normalization. That sum is stored in both
Y and R slots for later consumption. The observed final-sum bits match the independent
FP32-add reference exactly on both inputs.

Each complete run uses 63 serial dispatches through the stem, all 28 encoder layers
and both head attention/MLP blocks. The same two resident core images and contexts serve
every stage. Independently compiled new instruction layouts match their existing
executable/initialization payloads; attention remains 15,600 bytes per core and the
vector/MLP image 14,624. The extended arena contains 204,674,016 words. All constants
and instructions are resident before the first dispatch; integer token/type address
scheduling remains host work, with zero interstage host activation reads, writes or
syncs. Stopped-prefix observations supply only independent checks, never device inputs.

Both inputs run ten prefixes under two poisons. Direct operators, exact ReLU packing,
biased sums, residual bits, guards, immutable constants and all mutable-region poison
digests pass. The second attention's direct error on the fixture is
0.0002746739058112624 maximum absolute, relative L2 4.822021508363176e-06. These are
direct attention comparisons against the actual biased device QKV, not original-model
decision accuracy. The independent quantized-product reference still exposes
pointwise composition failures after both heads:

| Input | Final raw head-sum relative L2 | Bad elements | Maximum absolute error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Fixture, valid keys 91 | 0.005593189969658852 | 14,733 | 96.73394775390625 |
| AG News, valid keys 83 | 0.0054298886097967625 | 32,784 | 60.755615234375 |

Both complete-head runs retain six strict encoder-MLP failures and return exit 1 for
the unchanged numerical gates. These are diagnostics on two real inputs, not the full
frozen decision evaluation. The scorer, marker selection and action tail remain absent,
so neither model output is available yet. No complete-model accuracy or speed claim
follows from this checkpoint.

The [validation](../results/laya/heads_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes 99

transfer stays in bounds, every intended output word is covered, biased scatter
preserves residual slots, identity coefficients preserve padding, and empty/invalid

## Laya full device outputs: fixture qualification and first residual correction (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [corrected full-chain run](../results/laya/action_v2_normalized_residual_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log)
produces both model outputs, logits and action probabilities, on the NPU. It executes
token embedding, the complete encoder, both head blocks, marker selection and scoring,
logits masking, softmax/entropy/top-two features, and the action head. Three serialized
resident images share the same arena BO after full allocation-group/bank checks. The
complete path uses 66 dispatches, with zero interstage host activation reads, writes
or syncs. The host schedules integer token/marker addresses and supplies masks/counts;
it performs no floating activation gather, scorer, entropy or action computation that
feeds the device. CPU oracles are present in this qualification harness and inspect
separately stopped prefixes; this is not yet the production serving path.

The [first scorer run](../results/laya/scorer_v1_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log) and
[first full-output attempt](../results/laya/action_v1_full_fixture_desktop2_20261016.log)
pass their direct checks but inherit a graph-integration error: the stem preserves raw
embedding E as R, and the earlier composed reference assumes the same initial residual.
The exported first encoder Add consumes normalized embedding Y instead. Comparing with
the frozen original FP32 fixture exposed this shared error. Add a device-only bit-copy
command that keeps Y and seeds R from those same Y bits, then start the composed reference
from normalized Y too. The graph-contract check verifies the exact producer/consumer
edge before executing. Older logs and figures remain above with that limitation attached.

The [rebuild](../results/laya/full_rebuild_carry_desktop2_20261016.log) independently
compiles each new instruction layout and compares executable/initialization payloads
for its resident image. The corrected vector image occupies 14,992 bytes per core,
conservative stack bound 5,184; the new tail image 12,672 bytes with bound 4,448. Both
reserve 5,376 stack bytes, and the unchanged attention image retains its previous
audit. The [vector/carry probe](../results/laya/vector_v4_carry_operators_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes 48 comparisons, including exact Y-to-R copies and signed-zero bits. This fixes
integration without changing learned weights, quantization or numerical thresholds.

Marker positions follow the graph's minimum-zero clip; out-of-range positive indices
are rejected before address preparation. The scorer gathers selected rows through Shim
DMA, normalizes them, packs one matrix row group and executes its two biased products
with the original GELU. The action tail masks real options, excludes padded rows from
reductions, clips valid count to at least two and probabilities before logarithm, then
computes entropy, top-two margin and count scaling. It packs the device-produced CLS
row with those features for the two original action products and final softmax.

The [initial tail probe](../results/laya/tail_probe_v1_operators_desktop2_20261016.log)
fails eight of 26 comparisons. Vector lane-update arguments were reversed, so index
vectors for later score chunks did not advance; all-masked and padding cases exposed
the error. The [corrected probe](../results/laya/tail_probe_v2_fixed_indices_desktop2_20261016.log)
and [rebuilt-image repeat](../results/laya/tail_probe_v3_carry_image_desktop2_20261016.log)
each pass all 26 with unchanged gates. Cases include real option counts from small to
full extent, no valid markers, one valid marker, holes, ties, extreme scores and padding
above every real score. Logits masking and action-input BF16 packing match expected
bits; probability, logarithm and feature checks use their fixed numerical tolerances.

The [original FP32 comparison](../results/laya/full_fixture_fp32_comparison_desktop2_20261016.log)
checks the frozen model, external weights, item file and logits-file hashes before
reading the unlabelled fixture. Its frozen reference and corrected device logits are:

| Option | Frozen FP32 logit | Corrected NPU logit |
|---|---:|---:|
| First | 3.6975491046905518 | 3.683770179748535 |
| Second | -2.311758041381836 | -2.3182692527770996 |
| Third | -2.519770622253418 | -2.523902416229248 |

Maximum logit difference falls from 3.0837740898132324 with the wrong residual to
0.013778924942016602 after the correction; corrected relative L2 is
0.0031351891811937094. Device action probabilities are [0.9999999403953552, 0.0],
against [1.0, 0.0] from a fresh original-model CPU run. That action reference uses the
current ORT version rather than the frozen-logits version and does not replace the
frozen reference. These are one unlabelled fixture's outputs, not labelled accuracy.

Both poisons produce identical full outputs. Direct scorer/action and final composed
output comparisons against the independent quantized-product reference pass. Earlier
intermediate comparisons still fail: the corrected full run retains four strict MLP
failures and returns exit 1 with unchanged gates. The
[validation](../results/laya/full_model_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes 114
offline tests and the full syntax/import/shell gates, including address-patch limits,
every output word, residual carry and metadata rejection. All device processes release
idle while alive; no foreign context is observed. These are checks-only runs with CPU
oracles and large verification reads, so their durations establish no inference latency.
Production serving, native-arm registration, the frozen full-set decision/calibration
criteria and eligible paired whole-model speed remain unverified.

## Laya resident serving baseline: complete outputs, slow execution (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

`kernels/laya_transformer/native.py` reuses three device contexts and resident model
constants across calls. Each frame updates integer token/marker addresses, valid lengths,
question type and boolean option metadata, then executes the complete model with no CPU
neural operations. The initial residual remains the normalized embedding. Only logits
and action probabilities return to the host; static parameter packing is setup work.

[Serving qualification](../results/laya/native_serving_v1_probe_desktop2_20261016.log)
ran all three unlabelled fixtures and returned to the first fixture in the same session.
CPU neural/oracle functions and ONNX Runtime execution were patched to raise throughout
initialization and inference: zero calls occurred. Full and partial output readback were
bit-identical, as were repeated first-fixture results. All fixture output tolerances
passed. Partial readback transferred 16–24 bytes per frame instead of the full arena.
This checks-only qualification supplies no eligible latency measurement.

The [same-sitting benchmark](../results/laya/native_serving_v2_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log)
is timing-eligible, exits successfully, observes no foreign contention and confirms no
remaining hardware contexts. It uses the first unlabelled fixture, actual length 91,
original pinned weights, two warmups and five measured calls per configuration. Setup
is excluded. CPU uses ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 with eight threads and FP32; the device uses
the qualified BF16 matrix path with FP32 accumulation. These are different arithmetic
paths, with final output tolerances checked rather than bit-exact cross-device claims.

| Complete inference configuration | Median ms | Min–max ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| CPU, actual 91 tokens | 194.3114 | 190.3393–194.8332 |
| CPU, padded to 512 with attention mask | 5309.6317 | 5296.4347–5393.9701 |
| NPU, current fixed 512-token schedule | 2555.0765 | 2548.1006–2560.1271 |

The NPU is 13.1494 times slower than the actual-length CPU baseline. Padding CPU inputs
is a control, not the fair baseline for the speed goal. A separate instrumented frame
attributes 1356.9231 ms to encoder MLP stages and 1036.9860 ms to encoder attention,
projection and norm stages. Preparation is 0.6932 ms and readback 0.0521 ms in that frame;
these stage timings include driver waits and context transitions, not just core time.
The evidence points to device-stage work as the next optimization target. Shorter M/KV
schedules remain an unmeasured proposal, not a claimed speedup.

This baseline supersedes the earlier statement that serving and eligible timing were
absent. Native-arm preregistration and the complete frozen labelled decision/calibration
gates remain open. No labelled native class scores were produced by these experiments;
three unlabelled fixtures cannot establish model accuracy. Earlier intermediate
composition and strict MLP failures remain retained in the preceding sections.

## Laya shorter encoder MLP schedules: exact outputs, modest speedup (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

`bucket_mlp.py` selects an encoder MLP row bucket of 128, 256, 384 or 512 using the
actual input length. Weight banks, feature strides, arithmetic and resident vector
image remain unchanged. Only active row prefixes are written. Attention, embeddings
and heads still use the preceding fixed 512-token schedule. This is an experimental
complete-model runner, not an engine compiler feature or a general model API.

The [successful build](../results/laya/bucket_mlp_v3_build_desktop2_20261016.log)
independently checks all four layouts against the resident vector ELF/initialization
identity. The first two build attempts remain recorded: an
[unresolved relative subprocess path](../results/laya/bucket_mlp_v1_build_desktop2_20261016.log)
and an [audit tuple/list serialization mismatch](../results/laya/bucket_mlp_v2_build_desktop2_20261016.log).
Neither attempt ran the NPU; the corrections resolve output paths before subprocesses
and normalize audit serialization before comparison, without relaxing identity checks.

[Device qualification and paired timing](../results/laya/bucket_mlp_v1_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log)
alternate baseline and shortened complete-model calls in the same three contexts, with
resident constants and no arena reset. All 25 comparisons are bit-exact for both final
outputs: the three unlabelled fixtures and synthetic inputs spanning lengths 1–512,
including both sides of tile/bucket boundaries and repeated large-to-small transitions.
CPU neural/oracle functions are forbidden throughout session initialization and calls;
zero calls occur. This establishes tested schedule equivalence to the native baseline,
not frozen labelled accuracy or equivalence for every possible input.

| Complete-model path, 91-token fixture | Median ms | Min–max ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original fixed 512-token schedule | 2568.4374 | 2561.0245–2570.1286 |
| Shorter encoder MLP schedule | 1600.0193 | 1597.4431–1610.0899 |

Five paired measured calls per configuration alternate order after qualification has
warmed both paths. Setup is excluded; input preparation and final output readback remain
inside each measured call. The complete-model speedup is 1.6053 times. A separate
instrumented shortened frame spends 399.5067 ms in encoder MLP stages and 1206.5799 ms
in all other stages, including driver waits/context transitions. The wrapper records
exit 0, timing eligibility, no observed foreign contention and no contexts after close.
An offline validation process ran during earlier boundary qualification and had exited
before the paired timed calls. This is a same-session NPU comparison; the CPU timing in
the preceding section was not repeated in this run.

[Validation](../results/laya/bucket_mlp_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes 133
offline tests, the legacy syntax/import/shell gate and existing artifact/operator audits.
This improves the preceding serving baseline but remains slow. Shorter attention and
head schedules, native-arm preregistration, and the frozen full-set decision/calibration
gates remain open. No native labelled class scores were produced.

## Laya shorter encoder attention: exact outputs, CPU still faster (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

`bucket_attention.py` extends the preceding MLP row buckets to encoder QKV projection,
RoPE, attention, output projection and normalization. Physical feature and head pitches
remain unchanged. Query DMA skips inactive gaps between heads. Attention explicitly
consumes M/32 key/value blocks, all produced inside the selected M-token bucket; it
never reads untouched KV slots beyond that bucket. Embedding and head schedules remain
512 tokens. The new attention image reads its KV loop count from the existing control
field rather than using a hardcoded count.

The [build](../results/laya/bucket_attention_v2_build_desktop2_20261016.log) checks the
four row layouts share identical resident ELF/initialization images. Each core uses
15,648 code bytes and a conservative stack bound of 4,768 bytes inside its 4,864-byte
reservation. The vector image remains unchanged. A [prior build attempt](../results/laya/bucket_attention_v1_build_desktop2_20261016.log)
stopped before compilation because it selected an absent copied kernel object; the
successful build uses the audited repeated-layer object. No device run used that failed
attempt. The comparison runner retains the original attention context alongside the new
one, allocating four contexts in total so both schedules can alternate in one session.

[Fresh-session checks](../results/laya/bucket_attention_v1_fresh_short_desktop2_20261016.log)
start with shortened execution before any baseline populated padding. Both final outputs
match the original native baseline bit-for-bit on all three unlabelled fixtures. That

The [eligible same-sitting comparison](../results/laya/bucket_attention_v2_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log)
repeats fresh short execution and all 25 fixture/synthetic boundary comparisons from the
preceding experiment. All outputs remain bit-exact. CPU neural/oracle calls are forbidden
through native setup and inference, with zero calls observed. All model constants remain
resident, no activation arena reset occurs, and all 66 neural dispatches remain on the
NPU. A separate original-model CPU session is closed before native setup.

| Complete-model configuration, actual length 91 | Median ms | Min–max ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original fixed 512-token NPU schedule | 2566.9593 | 2560.6521–2571.9643 |
| Shorter encoder MLP only | 1595.0949 | 1593.3749–1604.4717 |
| Shorter encoder attention and MLP | 824.9203 | 809.4550–833.5963 |
| CPU, original model and actual length | 175.4385 | 174.1856–178.3842 |

Each configuration has five measured calls. NPU paths alternate order after boundary
qualification warmed them; CPU uses two warmups, ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 and eight threads.
Setup is excluded, while per-call preparation and final output readback are included.
CPU uses FP32 and NPU uses the qualified BF16 matrix path with FP32 accumulation;
fixture outputs satisfy the existing numerical comparison. The complete NPU speedup
over its fixed schedule is 3.1118 times, but it remains 4.7020 times slower than the
actual-length CPU. No other benchmark or compiler job ran during this comparison.

An instrumented shortened frame attributes 273.9261 ms to encoder attention/projection/
norm, 383.8343 ms to encoder MLP, and the remaining time primarily to fixed head stages.

records timing eligibility, exit 0, no observed foreign contention, and no remaining

passes 138 offline tests, the legacy syntax/import/shell gate and previous artifact audits.

This improves the preceding serving result; it does not establish the speed goal or

registering a native accuracy arm, and the full frozen decision/calibration gates remain
open. No native labelled class scores were produced.

## Laya GEMM compiler tuning: small overlapping timing change (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

An [offline object screen](../results/laya/gemm_codegen_v1_screen_desktop2_20261016.log)
compares the unchanged GEMM source under size and speed optimization. `gemm_tune.py`
then [builds a candidate vector image](../results/laya/gemm_tune_v1_o3_build_desktop2_20261016.log)
with only GEMM compiled at `-O3`; the five other object files are unchanged. The image
uses 15,328 code bytes per core. Physical buffer spans, control addresses and the original
runtime instruction bytes match the original vector image. This establishes its checked
ABI, not a numerical or performance result by itself.

[Fresh-short fixture checks](../results/laya/gemm_tune_v1_o3_fresh_short_desktop2_20261016.log)
are followed by a [timing-eligible same-session comparison](../results/laya/gemm_tune_v2_o3_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log).
Each uses all three unlabelled fixtures, both final outputs bit-exact to the native
baseline, CPU neural/oracle calls forbidden during native setup/inference, and zero such
calls. The tuned image executes encoder MLP stages only; stem, heads and all other
stages retain their previous images. The comparison keeps both vector images and both
attention images alive, for five contexts total, with 66 dispatches per complete frame.

| Complete-model path, 91-token fixture | Median ms | Min–max ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| Short encoder with original GEMM | 832.3829 | 815.3721–838.4884 |
| Short encoder with tuned MLP GEMM | 819.5820 | 804.7238–842.1869 |
| CPU, original model at actual length | 178.2744 | 172.2158–180.3299 |

The eligible run has nine measured calls per configuration, alternating NPU order after
fixture qualification. CPU uses two warmups, eight threads and ONNX Runtime 1.30.0;
its session closes before native setup. Setup is excluded and per-call preparation /
final readback included. CPU FP32 and NPU BF16 matrix arithmetic retain the preceding
qualifications. The measured median difference is small and the ranges overlap; this
experiment does not establish a repeatable substantial gain from compiler flags. The
tuned image remains a diagnostic candidate, not a replacement for the preceding
25-case-qualified shorter encoder. No full boundary or labelled accuracy run used it.

The wrapper records exit 0, timing eligibility, no observed foreign contention, and no
contexts after close. [Validation](../results/laya/gemm_tune_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes the existing 138 offline checks, legacy syntax/import/shell gate and previous
artifact/operator audits. Arithmetic, data traffic and synchronization contributions
remain unresolved; the next useful diagnostic separates phase costs before attributing
the remaining latency to a mechanism. Native accuracy preregistration and the complete
frozen decision/calibration gates remain open.

the preceding 25-case-qualified shorter encoder, not the compiler-tuning candidate.

The original item file, original FP32 logits and original preregistration remain
unchanged. The native addendum retains the original CPU reference session metadata;
its separate `native_policy` defines actual device execution: batch one, four contexts,

C0 now checks this explicit native artifact/source map against its committed registration
before and after scoring. C1–C5 retain their original thresholds and definitions: pooled

No calibration fitting or temperature changes are allowed.

strict MLP failures remain retained; registration does not resolve them.

The final-output development set comprises the three unlabelled fixtures. An earlier
labelled item was used only for intermediate activation qualification before the final

native C0–C5 results remain pending. This is a registration milestone, not an accuracy

## Laya deeper encoder buffering reduces complete latency (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [MLP-only fresh qualification](../results/laya/mlp_fifo_v1_double_m128_fresh_desktop2_20261016.log)
preserves both outputs bit-for-bit on three unlabelled fixtures, with zero CPU neural/oracle
calls. Its [eligible seven-repetition comparison](../results/laya/mlp_fifo_v1_double_m128_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log)
measures original short encoder 820.7809 ms versus buffered MLP 726.9808 ms median.
The candidate removes dead attention buffers and doubles the query/KV paths while keeping
the complete original arithmetic object byte-identical. This establishes the combined
plumbing change's gain; it does not isolate each FIFO's contribution.

The [attention-only fresh qualification](../results/laya/attention_fifo_v1_double_m128_fresh_desktop2_20261016.log)
also preserves both fixture outputs exactly. Its checks-only counters are timing-ineligible.
The [first combined attempt](../results/laya/buffered_v1_double_m128_boundaries_desktop2_20261016.log)
fails when creating a sixth context, before combined inference. No contexts remain after
cleanup. This is an observed context-creation failure, not proof of a universal silicon limit.

`compact_attention.py` recompiles the unchanged full head stream for the existing
variable-KV context, explicitly selecting sixteen KV blocks. Its
[build](../results/laya/compact_attention_v1_build_desktop2_20261016.log) proves the linked
core programs and initialization match that context. `buffered_probe.py` first compares
actual original-context fixture outputs before/after consolidation, then releases the
old attention context. It retains full allocation groups, checks bank compatibility and
uses each candidate's own physical control map and compiled instruction stream.

The [combined boundary qualification](../results/laya/buffered_v2_compact_m128_boundaries_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes all 25 complete-output comparisons bit-for-bit, including repeated lengths and
transitions through all row buckets. M128 alone selects the deeper encoder buffers;
other buckets retain original short schedules. The full head stream is unchanged apart
from its context/count plumbing. Setup consolidation independently passes on all three
unlabelled fixtures. CPU neural/oracle calls are forbidden and zero are observed.

The [eligible seven-repetition comparison](../results/laya/buffered_v3_compact_m128_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log)
alternates arm order within one resident session. All arms share the same context set,
resident weights, request and full output readback policy. Setup is excluded.

| Complete-model arm, fixture length 91 | Median ms | Observed range ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full-512 encoder schedule, consolidated attention context | 2550.2073 | 2544.9696–2559.1020 |
| Original short encoder | 832.5928 | 803.1979–836.0277 |
| MLP buffering/pruning alone | 723.7846 | 694.7999–742.7985 |
| Attention buffering alone | 756.9851 | 745.0018–779.1092 |
| Both encoder buffering changes | 669.3234 | 635.9564–678.4057 |
| CPU FP32 at actual token length, same sitting | 178.4173 | 176.0430–179.4473 |

The combined arm reduces median latency by 19.61% against the original short arm and is
3.8101 times faster than the full-512 schedule. It remains 3.7514 times slower than CPU.
Execution uses five contexts and 66 dispatches per frame, with zero CPU neural/oracle
calls and device idle after close. The wrapper records `timing_eligible: true` and no
foreign contention. The CPU comparison remains FP32 versus BF16 matrix operands with
FP32 accumulation on the NPU; this is fixture speed, not a full-dataset latency average.

The [buffered-arm registration](../results/laya/buffered_accuracy_v1_prereg_desktop2_20261016.json)
and [registration log](../results/laya/buffered_accuracy_v1_registration_desktop2_20261016.log)
freeze 176 source/artifact hashes before this arm scores labelled final outputs. It
retains original items, FP32 logits and C1–C5, and additionally requires full scored
output bit equivalence to the already qualified native arm. Prior native outcomes have
been observed; this is explicitly not a new independent held-out study. Full buffered
accuracy is pending, so the original qualified accuracy arm remains available unchanged.

**Follow-up:** the buffered arm subsequently passes the complete frozen gates and full
native output bit equivalence; see [the completed run](#laya-buffered-native-accuracy-c0c5-and-full-bit-equivalence-pass-2026-10-16-desktop-2).

[Validation](../results/laya/buffered_accuracy_v1_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes

[initial](../results/laya/buffered_geglu_v1_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) and

validation stages are retained. No precision, learned weights or accuracy criteria change.

## Laya dedicated GeGLU compiler candidate (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

`geglu_tune.py` builds a dedicated MLP image from unchanged `mlp.cc`, retaining the
original GEMM, dispatch, normalization and finish objects. It removes unreachable
attention code/buffers and unused stem/head dispatches, leaving the existing MLP packet
and runtime emitter. The [O3 build](../results/laya/geglu_tune_v1_o3_build_desktop2_20261016.log)

Both conservative stack bounds are 3,456 bytes within the explicit 5,376-byte reservation.

Both [O3](../results/laya/geglu_tune_v1_o3_m128_fresh_desktop2_20261016.log) and
[Oz](../results/laya/geglu_tune_v2_oz_m128_control_desktop2_20261016.log) preserve full
logits and action probabilities exactly on the three unlabelled fixtures, with no CPU
neural/oracle calls and idle device after close. These runs are checks-only and
timing-ineligible; neither a qualified speedup nor full frozen accuracy is established.
The dedicated dispatch and compiler changes are separate from the measured buffering arm.
