## Laya lookup fixtures pass; compact DMA packing fails on device (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [GELU lookup fixture run](../results/laya/geglu_lut_v1_fresh_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes the existing development numerical gates on three unlabelled fixtures. Action
probabilities remain bit-exact; logits change, with maximum absolute differences
0.011100530624389648, 0.02213609218597412 and 0.059857845306396484 against the original
short native arm. Relative L2 differences are 0.002235378371551633,
0.00980337057262659 and 0.012564300559461117. The run observes zero CPU neural/oracle
calls, five contexts, 66 dispatches and an idle device after close. It uses full heads.
Its checks-only counters are timing-ineligible and establish no serving speed claim.
The lookup approximation still requires a separate registration and complete frozen
C0–C5 validation; the qualified buffered arm's full accuracy cannot be inherited.

The [split-descriptor compact-pack run](../results/laya/compact_pack_v1_fresh_desktop2_20261016.log)
fails at the first encoder attention dispatch after the native wait, then exits 139.
No candidate output comparison completes. The post-process device report shows no
active contexts. A subsequent [lookup/short-head combination attempt](../results/laya/optimized_lut_head_v1_fresh_desktop2_20261016.log)
fails during initial context creation with `0xc01e0009`, before inference. That attempt
does not test the combination's arithmetic or performance. Hardware testing is held
for driver recovery; the compact candidate is unqualified and must not be reused as a
working configuration. Descriptor ordering, packet boundaries and synchronization
remain possible causes; the timeout alone establishes none of them.

A separately versioned wide-packet alternative sends each normalization packet through
one Shim descriptor. It gathers FP32 rows of width 66, consumes the first 64 values and
retains the original live payload and source pitches for other operations. The
[first build](../results/laya/compact_pack_wide_v1_build_desktop2_20261016.log) fails a
KV type mismatch; the [corrected build](../results/laya/compact_pack_wide_v2_build_desktop2_20261016.log)
updates both compiler KV-size bindings and passes code/stack/span audits: 15,792 code
bytes and a 4,672-byte stack bound within the unchanged reservation. It has never run
on hardware. `optimized_probe.py` prepares serialized combinations with shorter heads,
the polynomial or lookup MLP, and this optional wide-packet attention image, replacing
the prior candidate context before allocating another one.

The [offline validation](../results/laya/optimized_candidates_v1_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
checks packet coverage, preserved source strides and unused words, compiler-global
restoration, and the existing offline suite and legacy import/syntax gates. Offline
success provides no evidence that either compact DMA scheme executes correctly.

The scoring run is timing-ineligible because separate offline work ran concurrently;

comes from its own eligible comparison and applies to this now accuracy-qualified arm.

The original native, buffered and lookup arms reuse the same frozen labelled set.
After the first complete native score, its outcomes were known; the later buffered
and lookup results are re-validations on that known set, not independent held-out
tests. Passing the unchanged gates preserves the result without establishing a new
held-out accuracy claim.

Performance against the hybrid remains unmeasured at matching row schedules. The
earlier native speedups compare native schedules with each other; they do not prove

## Laya native versus hybrid at matched and serving schedules (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

Native loses to hybrid at matched 512-row schedules. For the same logical 91-token
request, the qualified lookup/short-head serving arm is faster than the current
hybrid, whose closest supported row schedule is 512. The qualified buffered arm with
full heads remains slower than hybrid. This separates a serving-configuration gain
from a claim that moving the same full schedule onto the NPU made it faster.

The [registered protocol](../results/laya/native_hybrid_compare_v1_prereg_desktop2_20261016.json)
was committed before comparison inference, SHA256
`bb65c96e85b3886e22644978e937c3a72f9c453a21444af3726b1b4bec8625e2`.
A [bounded qualification](../results/laya/native_hybrid_compare_v1_qualification_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes before the [eligible same-sitting comparison](../results/laya/native_hybrid_compare_v1_same_sitting_desktop2_20261016.log).
Three rounds rotate all four profiles; each profile warms twice and measures five
complete inferences, excluding model/session setup. All use the same first unlabelled
fixture and output/decision checks against CPU FP32. Reported profile medians aggregate
the 15 timed samples per arm. Input tokenization is outside inference timing.

| Profile | Executed row schedule | Median ms | Observed sample range ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Existing hybrid | 512 | 620.9457 | 616.3143–626.7880 |
| Native matched full schedule | 512 encoder and heads | 2558.9248 | 2499.2072–2566.3774 |
| Qualified buffered native | M128 encoder, full heads | 693.2183 | 647.8893–703.6357 |
| Qualified lookup/short-head native | M128 encoder and heads | 509.2963 | 453.6631–514.8653 |

The current `tools/laya_hybrid.py` fixes `SEQ=512`, allocates fixed-size A/C buffers,
and sends shorter activations to its host product branch. This comparison neither
patches that value nor compiles new transactions. Both matched-512 profiles receive
the identical right-padded 91-token input and mask. Native's full-schedule control
uses its original full-512 instructions; the other native arms use their qualified
serving policies. No matched-M128 hybrid result exists, so the serving gain includes
row bucketing and must not be attributed solely to eliminating host neural segments.
The earlier native speedup subjects compared against native's slower full schedule;
they did not establish a win over the pre-existing hybrid.

Actual hybrid counters confirm 118 NPU products, two host products and 121 CPU segment
calls per inference, including each profile's warmups. Native profiles observe zero
CPU neural/oracle calls, five contexts and 66 dispatches per inference. Hybrid uses
one context. Profiles are serialized, with idle checks before and after each, and
the process leaves no contexts after close. The wrapper records no foreign contention
and `timing_eligible: true`. Registered source/artifact identities match at both ends.

CPU measurements are interleaved before the first profile and after every profile:
13 blocks, each with actual-length and padded inputs, three timed samples after two
warmups, and rotating thread/spinning configurations. Sessions are released before
NPU execution. The following ranges are across block medians, not individual samples.

| CPU FP32 configuration | Input rows | Range of block medians ms | Registered stability test |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| One thread, spinning disabled | 91 | 513.8980–548.8352 | PASS |
| One thread, spinning disabled | 512 | 3278.9098–3403.3327 | PASS |
| Eight threads, spinning disabled | 91 | 129.2672–193.9409 | FAIL |
| Eight threads, spinning disabled | 512 | 820.2148–1273.3489 | FAIL |
| Eight threads, default spinning | 91 | 105.4451–180.2010 | FAIL |
| Eight threads, default spinning | 512 | 810.4175–1474.6125 | FAIL |

The one-thread controls stay within the preregistered maximum/minimum block-median
ratio of 1.10; all eight-thread controls exceed it, especially in the final CPU block.
System CPU load samples, process CPU seconds and native thread counts are retained.
Disabling spinning does not remove the observed instability. Its cause remains
unexplained: these observations do not establish clock, thermal, affinity, memory or
background-work causality. All NPU/CPU performance ratios are withheld as registered.
The earlier two-bracket CPU ratio is not an accepted result either.

Verbose output stays in ignored `scratch/`. The committed summary records the raw
SHA256 `d77ba78f5db5317edda1436b05fd24b99996a5596c50b6da5e7a750d1cab6d0e`,
protocol identity, per-profile samples/load, correctness checks, idle witnesses and
terminal eligibility. These measurements do not relax the original accuracy gates
or establish a whole-model speed target beyond this fixture and its named schedules.

## Laya guarded single-BD packing primitive (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [bounded original and candidate runs](../results/laya/pack_primitive_v1_device_desktop2_20261016.log)
qualify a packing-only primitive on column zero, four broadcast cores and one feature
group. They use independent processes, one context each, with the original passing
before the candidate is run. This is synthetic primitive qualification, not complete
Laya inference or a speed measurement. The full-model registered artifacts and gates
remain unchanged.

Each variant passes six cases: three distinct random inputs, each with two alternating
output poisons. Inputs also contain positive and negative round-to-even ties. Every
bit in all four complete output packets matches an independent NumPy BF16 packing
reference, including expected packet filler. Input bytes remain unchanged, and every
output word outside the designated four-packet region retains its poison. The checks
cover complete writes, payload order, input/output guards and repeated dispatches.
Both bounded wrappers exit normally and record an idle device before and after; the
process also checks idle after releasing its context while it remains alive.

[Offline gates](DECISIONS.md#laya-packing-primitive-transport-gates-2026-10-16-desktop-2)
precede hardware execution. The original consumes 128 full-row KV objects; the single-BD
candidate consumes four FP32[32,66] objects, using the first 64 values in each row.
The checked initialization covers 2,284 register traces, 424 lock writes and 48
normalized KV descriptors. Only audited buffer relocation and the KV width differ;
query/output descriptors and all remaining descriptor/lock fields retain their
checked behavior. The candidate sends one complete object per descriptor iteration.
This is a different transfer scheme from the earlier failed split-packet experiment.

[Validation](../results/laya/pack_primitive_v1_validation_desktop2_20261016.log)
passes 36 offline/privacy checks and the legacy syntax/import/shell gate. New checks
include all-word packing identities, decoder framing, and corruption of TLAST, packet
length, repeat count and lock initialization. The committed device summary retains
both raw hashes; verbose raw logs stay in ignored scratch.

These checks-only runs are **timing-ineligible**. They establish exact guarded output
for the tested feature group and column. Other features/columns, complete attention,
full-model accuracy and any end-to-end speed gain remain unqualified for this candidate.
A bounded layer integration and expanded coverage precede its full-model comparison.

## Laya L1-resident GEMM diagnostic qualifies after signed-zero oracle fix (2026-10-16, Desktop 2)

The [L1 diagnostic qualification](../results/laya/l1_gemm_v3_qualification_desktop2_20261016.log)
places Laya's unchanged serving GEMM object and the specialized object in the
existing one-core L1 harness, alongside an empty-call control. All use the same
32-by-64-by-64 tiled operands, three FIFO allocations and compiled transaction
bytes. The repeated call loop contains no DMA. This removes streamed operand
transfers from the per-call slope, but changes placement relative to serving and
cannot alone explain complete-inference latency.

The first two attempts stopped on the zero-call bit check. The captured diagnostic
identifies a reference bug: multiplying a negative CPU product by zero manufactured
negative-zero expected bits; the core correctly returned its explicit positive-zero
initialization. Actual words are zero, whereas the failing expected words are
2,147,483,648. No kernel arithmetic or serving accuracy gate changes. Both failed
attempts and the capture hash remain in the record. The corrected reference passes
zero, one and three calls on all three images, checking every output bit, unchanged
inputs and output-tail guards. Processes exit zero and release all contexts. These
qualification wall times are ineligible for performance claims.

Before device use, offline checks validate every Shim word address and completion
token, whole FIFO objects, six hardware lock initializations and three compiled
core DMA lock fields per image. All images have identical SRAM spans and transport;
code and conservative stack bounds fit their reserved memory. The
[19 offline/privacy checks](../results/laya/l1_gemm_v3_offline_tests_desktop2_20261016.log)
include the signed-zero regression and corrupted packet/completion rejection;
[legacy validation](../results/laya/l1_gemm_v3_validation_desktop2_20261016.log) passes.
The original serving image and frozen decision/accuracy gates remain unchanged.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qualified unsplit control | 66 | 450.3734 | 396.2272–474.1138 |
| Diagnostic split MLPs | 150 | 495.7704 | 398.2033–524.8756 |

## Five-row maps on the existing core: a 5x20 sensor model compiles whole and layer-exact, and is 1.3x slower than one CPU thread (2026-09-28, Desktop 2)

hipnet v0 is an untrained hip-rotation estimator from a separate project, designed from Ignition's model guide. Its
feature map is one 5x20 tile: rows are five tracker groups, columns twenty frames at 30 Hz, 32 or 64 channels. It
uses only 3x3 and 1x1 convolutions, ReLU and residual adds, and its raw output is decoded on the host. Two variants
ask a question each: `k5` puts 5x5 convolutions in the blocks, `relu_after_add` puts a ReLU after each add.

- **Quantization:** plain XINT8, Quark 0.11rc1 `get_default_config("XINT8")` (CLE on), on the project's 64
  calibration frames. Every scale is a power of two, activations are uint8 at zero point 128, and the input scale is
  2^-7. On ORT CPU the QDQ output is within 0.0126 of FP32 at the readout, whose magnitude is 0.18-0.20: no
  collapse. The models are untrained, so this is not accuracy.
- **Tools:** `tools/hipnet_probe_silicon.py` (exactness and the sitting), `tools/hipnet_probe_offline.py` (lowering,
  schedule emulation, ORT intermediates) and `tools/schedule_fingerprint.py` (the identical-schedule check). The
  models, containers and calibration frames are the other project's and are not in this repository.

**`main` (`de276fb`) refuses all three.** The base and `k5` models stop at scheduling with
`ValueError: a 5-pixel map is smaller than one 20-pixel tile`. A core computes a 5x20 tile, but the scheduler issues
a column of four cores stacked five rows apart as one quad, which covers twenty rows. `relu_after_add` stops earlier,
in lowering: `add has 0 QuantizeLinear consumers`, because Quark writes Add -> Relu -> QuantizeLinear
([`hipnet_probe_5x20_main_refusals_desktop2_20260928.log`](../results/aie/hipnet_probe_5x20_main_refusals_desktop2_20260928.log)).

**`b58ea8f` (branch `worktree-hipnet-short-map`, not on `main`) takes both, with no kernel change.**
- A tensor exactly five rows tall reserves four copies of its layout. Core row r of the quad reads copy r of its
  input and drains into copy r of its output. Copy 0 is the tensor at its usual base, so the runtime is unchanged;
  copies 1-3 hold junk. The workspace for those tensors is 4x
  ([DECISIONS](DECISIONS.md#five-row-maps-are-scheduled-on-replicas-not-on-a-stride-0-quad-2026-09-28)).
- ReLU after an add becomes the residual packet's post-add epilogue, the same `max(q, 128)` constants a
  convolution's ReLU uses. No shipped model uses that epilogue.
- Heights 10 and 15 still refuse.
- Nothing else moves. YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s and SESR M7 hash identically under `de276fb` and `b58ea8f`, with workspace
  reuse on and off: every placement, every column program and the weight packets.

**Exact on silicon.** The ONNX graph's 27 compute nodes (33 in `relu_after_add`) lower to 14 layers:
- each Conv is a layer, with its ReLU as the layer's epilogue;
- each Add is the second convolution's RESIDUAL step, with the ReLU after it (`relu_after_add`) as the post-add
  epilogue;
- 0 host segments.

Over 16 calibration frames per container:

| Model | Reuse-free container | Default container | Output vs ORT CPU on the QDQ model | Activation packets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hipnet_v0 | 14/14 layers exact | 5/5 readable exact, 9/9 reused slots hold their final tenant | 0 mismatches | 252 |
| hipnet_v0_k5 | 14/14 | 5/5, 9/9 | 0 | 828 |
| hipnet_v0_relu_after_add | 14/14 | 5/5, 9/9 | 0 | 252 |

Offline, the emulated schedule equals the reference at every layer in both workspace modes. The reference equals ORT
CPU's uint8 intermediates at every layer
([`hipnet_probe_5x20_offline_desktop2_20260928.log`](../results/aie/hipnet_probe_5x20_offline_desktop2_20260928.log)).
The containers make 0 ONNX Runtime calls, counted in the harness.

**The sitting.** Three passes, arms interleaved per model, 50 warm-up and 1,000 timed calls per block, NPU pmode
`default`, xrt-smi idle before and after
([`hipnet_probe_5x20_desktop2_20260928T2211Z.log`](../results/aie/hipnet_probe_5x20_desktop2_20260928T2211Z.log)).
- "NPU call" is what a caller pays: float32 [1,32,5,20] in, quantize, stage, dispatch, read back, dequantize.
- The CPU arms are ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 on one intra-op and one inter-op thread.

| Median over the 3 passes (ms) | NPU dispatch | NPU call | CPU FP32 | CPU QDQ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hipnet_v0 | 0.6514-0.6532 | **0.7253-0.7260** | 0.5535-0.5656 | 0.9602-0.9640 |
| hipnet_v0_k5 | 1.4421-1.4432 | **1.5377-1.5394** | 1.4333-1.4474 | 2.4806-2.4899 |
| hipnet_v0_relu_after_add | 0.6665-0.6680 | **0.7401-0.7440** | 0.5540-0.5696 | 0.9903-0.9998 |

- **The NPU is slower than one CPU thread on this model.** An NPU call is 1.28-1.31x the CPU's FP32 time on the base
  model, 1.31-1.34x on `relu_after_add` and 1.06-1.07x on `k5` (DERIVED, per pass). It beats the same int8 graph
  on the CPU by 1.32-1.34x (1.61-1.62x on `k5`).
- **It costs the host little CPU time.** Process CPU time per NPU call was 0.0469-0.1406 ms across the nine blocks,
  against 0.5625-0.5781 ms per FP32 call on the base model. `process_time` ticks at 15.6 ms on Windows, so 1,000
  calls resolve it to about 0.016 ms: read that as under 0.15 ms, not as a per-pass figure.
- **`k5` costs 2.2x the base model's dispatch** and moves 828 activation packets to its 252. That fits one packet
  per 8 input channels for a 5x5 convolution, but nothing else was held fixed, so it is not isolated.
- **Why 14 layers of 5x20 take 0.65 ms of dispatch** (about 47 us per layer, DERIVED) is unexplained. Nothing here
  separates per-layer cost from transfer.
- The p99 of an NPU call is 0.8145-0.8242 ms on the base model, against 0.7410-0.9023 for the CPU.

**Not run:**
- accuracy (the models are untrained);
- the reuse-free containers' latency;
- AMD's VitisAI EP on these models;
- the laptop's Hawk Point NPU;
- energy;
- heights 10 and 15;
- the stride-0 alternative to replicas (not attempted:
  [DECISIONS](DECISIONS.md#five-row-maps-are-scheduled-on-replicas-not-on-a-stride-0-quad-2026-09-28)).

**Since measured:** the same model redesigned at 20x20 has the same schedule size and the same dispatch, and its NPU
call is 3.1x faster than one CPU thread
([Twenty rows cost the NPU what five did](#twenty-rows-cost-the-npu-what-five-did-the-same-sensor-model-at-20x20-is-31x-faster-than-one-cpu-thread-on-main-2026-09-28-desktop-2)).

## Twenty rows cost the NPU what five did: the same sensor model at 20x20 is 3.1x faster than one CPU thread, on `main` (2026-09-28, Desktop 2)

hipnet v2 is the other project's redesign after the five-row result
([above](#five-row-maps-on-the-existing-core-a-5x20-sensor-model-compiles-whole-and-layer-exact-and-is-13x-slower-than-one-cpu-thread-2026-09-28-desktop-2)).
The map is 20x20: one row per body tracker, twenty frames at 30 Hz, 32 or 64 channels. The 12 rows with no input
tracker are zero by design, and the model is built for that layout. The blocks are the same; there are two variants,
the base and `k5`, and no `relu_after_add`. Everything ran on `main` (`de276fb`), unmodified: a 20-row map needs no
branch.

- **Quantization:** the same plain XINT8 preset and 64 calibration frames. Every scale is a power of two,
  activations are uint8 at zero point 128, and the input scale is 2^-7. At the readout (the hip row), the QDQ output
  on ORT CPU is within 0.0070 of FP32 (0.0066 for `k5`), against a readout magnitude of 0.15-0.18. The models are
  untrained, so this is not accuracy.
- **Tools:** `tools/hipnet_probe_silicon.py` and `tools/hipnet_probe_offline.py`, as for five rows. The offline tool
  now reads `replicas` with a default, so it runs against `main`'s `Placement`. The quantize step now takes each
  model's readout from its sidecar. `tools/schedule_fingerprint.py` was not rerun: nothing on `main` changed.
- **`main` compiles both** to 14 layers, 0 on the host, 27 rounds. `ignite-compile --task segment` then exits 1 after
  writing the container, on a `KeyError: 'transform'` in its summary print. `b58ea8f` fixes that print
  ([`hipnet_probe_20x20_offline_desktop2_20260928.log`](../results/aie/hipnet_probe_20x20_offline_desktop2_20260928.log)).

**Exact on silicon.** Over 16 calibration frames per container, xrt-smi idle before and after, pmode `default`
([`hipnet_probe_20x20_desktop2_20260928T2249Z.log`](../results/aie/hipnet_probe_20x20_desktop2_20260928T2249Z.log)):

| Model | Reuse-free container | Default container | Output vs ORT CPU on the QDQ model | Activation packets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hipnet_v0 (20x20) | 14/14 layers exact | 5/5 readable exact, 9/9 reused slots hold their final tenant | 0 mismatches | 252 |
| hipnet_v0_k5 (20x20) | 14/14 | 5/5, 9/9 | 0 | 828 |

Offline, the emulated schedule equals the reference at every layer in both workspace modes, and the reference equals
ORT CPU's uint8 intermediates at every layer. The containers make 0 ONNX Runtime calls, counted in the harness.

**The sitting.** Same method as the five-row sitting: three passes, arms interleaved per model, 50 warm-up and 1,000
timed calls per block. "NPU call" is float32 [1,32,20,20] in to float32 out. The CPU arms are ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 on
one intra-op and one inter-op thread.

| Median over the 3 passes (ms) | NPU dispatch | NPU call | CPU FP32 | CPU QDQ | CPU FP32 / NPU call, per pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hipnet_v0 (20x20) | 0.6500-0.6511 | **0.7492-0.7518** | 2.3041-2.3204 | 3.2167-3.2393 | 3.08-3.09x |
| hipnet_v0_k5 (20x20) | 1.4433-1.4465 | **1.5690-1.5699** | 6.8331-6.8833 | 8.5556-8.5935 | 4.36-4.38x |

- **At 20 rows the NPU wins on latency.** Against the int8 graph on the CPU the NPU call is 4.28-4.32x faster
  (5.45-5.47x for `k5`, DERIVED, per pass).
- **It still costs the host little CPU.** Process CPU time per NPU call was 0.0938-0.1875 ms across the six blocks,
  against 2.3438-2.3594 ms per FP32 call on the base model and 6.9375-7.0000 on `k5`. The 15.6 ms `process_time`
  tick applies as before.
- **Twenty rows cost the NPU what five did.**
  - At compile time, v2 matches the five-row v1 containers exactly: 27 rounds, 252 activation packets (828 for
    `k5`), 18,148 instruction bytes (14,740) and 596,736 weight-packet bytes (1,960,704), in both sittings' JSON.
  - Only egress grows, from 3,200 to 12,800 B. Equal sizes are not equal instructions: the five-row column programs
    carry replica offsets.
  - Dispatch reads 0.6500-0.6511 ms against v1's 0.6514-0.6532 (`k5` 1.4433-1.4465 against 1.4421-1.4432). The two
    sittings are 38 minutes apart (22:11Z and 22:49Z), on the same machine and pmode with the NPU idle. That agreement
    is consistent with the schedule; it is not a same-sitting comparison.
  - The NPU call grew from 0.7253-0.7260 to 0.7492-0.7518 ms. That is consistent with staging and reading back four
    times the data, but it was not isolated.
- **So a five-row map pays for twenty.** Replicas keep all four core rows of a quad busy, three of them on junk
  copies ([DECISIONS](DECISIONS.md#five-row-maps-are-scheduled-on-replicas-not-on-a-stride-0-quad-2026-09-28)).
  A real 20-row map puts those rows to work at the same dispatch, while the CPU's FP32 time grows about 4x, as the
  multiply-adds do. That is the whole difference between 1.3x slower and 3.1x faster.
- **The 0.65 ms of dispatch does not depend on map height** between 5 and 20 rows. Why 14 layers take that long is
  still unexplained.
- **5x5 widens the lead.** `k5` costs 2.2x the base model's dispatch on the NPU, but 2.94-2.98x its time on the CPU
  (DERIVED, per pass).
- **Unexplained:** `k5`'s dispatch p99 is 1.9457-1.9717 ms here, against 1.4939-1.4973 in the five-row sitting, with
  medians within 0.4%. The base model's p99 did not move (0.6981-0.7024 against 0.7022-0.7138).

**Not run:**
- accuracy (the models are untrained);
- the reuse-free containers' latency;
- AMD's VitisAI EP on these models;
- the laptop's Hawk Point NPU;
- energy;
- a same-sitting run of the five-row and twenty-row containers.

## Standalone BF16 transformer primitives (2026-10-18, Desktop 2)

[`kernels/transformer_bf16/`](../kernels/transformer_bf16/README.md) extracts reusable
single-token BF16 vector projections, RMSNorm, supplied-factor rotary encoding,
streamed softmax, gated tanh GELU, residual/scaling and deterministic top-k from
the decoder prototype. It uses the native `ignite_xdna.runtime.driver` harness,
not ONNX Runtime. Model-specific weights, cache-window rules and orchestration
remain in the consuming application. The graph compiler and `.ignite` operator
vocabulary are unchanged.

**MEASURED, correctness only:** the bounded
[device check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_checks_20261018_v2.log) passed all
21 operation cases across seeds 11, 29 and 83, using independent PyTorch BF16
references. [Structured evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_checks_20261018.json)
retains source hashes, criteria, per-case errors and completed dispatch witnesses.
The GELU table's CPU preparation checks every one of the 65,280 finite BF16 bit
patterns; that is exhaustive CPU table validation, not exhaustive NPU execution.
Both pre/post device witnesses are idle. The wrapper marks the run timing-ineligible.

The [first attempt](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_checks_20261018.log) stopped
before device execution: a relative cache path was interpreted again from the
build directory. Resolving the cache/build directory before compilation fixes it;
the failed attempt is retained. The passing run uses the corrected sources.

This establishes a reusable research baseline with per-operation host packing
and context creation. It does not establish fused execution, whole-model accuracy,
compiler BF16 support, serving latency or a hybrid GPU/NPU speedup.

The consuming decoder workspace now imports `Bf16Ops` from this repository.
A separate [bounded composition check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_composed_attention_20261018.log)
passed all 16 selected attention cases: the four layers of E2B and E4B, each
with shared-cache lengths 37 and 8192. Query projection, RMSNorm, rotary
encoding, query-key products, softmax, probability-value products and output
projection all consume the preceding NPU output, with no reference substitution.
Both idle witnesses pass and the run is timing-ineligible. These are synthetic
target-state fixtures, not a complete decoder, agent evaluation or serving result.

### Complete draft composition and cached transport

**MEASURED, failed full-draft qualification:** the consumer now composes all four
assistant layers, final normalization, post-projection and the original clustered
BF16 vocabulary head. The [original GEMV attempt](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_complete_draft_20261018.log)
passes its first synthetic case but fails the next under the frozen relative-L2
limit 0.01 and maximum-error/reference-RMS limit 0.05. A traced repeat locates
small local dot-product rounding differences that amplify through later layers.
No CPU intermediate is substituted into the NPU computation.

The optional `precise_projection=True` implementation uses BF16 operands and
compensated FP32 accumulation, with one BF16 output rounding. It
[fixes the first failing case](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_compensated_draft_first_20261018.log),
but the [complete 24-case run](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_compensated_draft_full_20261018.log)
still passes only 18 numerical cases. Greedy tokens match in 23 cases; this
diagnostic does not override the six failed numerical cases. The run covers
both assistants, seeds 11/29/83, cache lengths 1/37/513/8192, and positions
0/36/8191/32767. Position 32767 does **not** mean a populated 32K cache.
[Structured evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_complete_draft_20261018.json)
preserves source identities, stage errors and all 2376 completed dispatches
from the 24-case run. All checks are synthetic target states; no target acceptance,
agent behavior, hybrid speedup or serving readiness is established.

**MEASURED, transport checks only:** `PacketSession` retains at most two complete
images and reuses their instruction/data BOs. The caller reserves exclusive NPU
use throughout the session; idle checks bracket it and the bounded wrapper
monitors ownership. This removes the per-operation idle-query subprocess and
retains contexts until eviction or explicit exit. It remains synchronous, with
host packing and round trips between operations.
The [cached transport check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_cached_transport_20261018.log)
passes 28 operation checks: three distinct inputs and an exact repeat of the first
for each of seven operations, including compensated projections. It records 21
cache hits, seven created contexts, five evictions and empty context state after
exit. Replays are bit-identical, input BOs are unchanged and output guards pass.
The [structured report](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_cached_transport_20261018.json)
records the criteria, source hashes and dispatch witnesses. Both idle witnesses
pass; timing is ineligible. This does not establish whole-draft qualification.

The [cached complete-step check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_cached_complete_draft_20261018.log)
passes four selected cases: E2B and E4B at cache lengths 37 and 513, seed 11.
Each complete step has 99 dispatches, 54 context creations, 45 cache hits and
52 evictions; all owned contexts are released. These cases already passed with
compensated accumulation in the uncached run. This is not a rerun or reversal of
the failed 24-case qualification. [Structured evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_cached_complete_draft_20261018.json)
retains the exact per-stage metrics and source identities. The final case's
diagnostic wall time is still about 2.8 seconds; it is a checks-only observation,
not a serving benchmark. The number of context creations identifies a remaining
transport cost before this could approach realtime use.

## BF16 packet dispatcher and real target inputs (2026-10-18, Desktop 2)

The standalone BF16 package now has a packet-opcode dispatcher containing all
seven operations in one core program. This shares program code while retaining
host round trips between operations; it is not a fused decoder graph. The
[first -O3 build](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_dispatch_compile_20261018.log)
fails program loading at 16,976 bytes, above the 16 KiB limit. The
[size-optimized build](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_dispatch_compile_20261018_v2.log)
fits at 12,768 bytes with recorded stack frames and nonoverlapping SRAM.
Limits were not raised.

Context sharing requires byte-identical PDI, kernel argument metadata and memory
topology, all recorded and checked at image admission. Equal ELF files alone are
insufficient. Each context owns its instruction/data BOs using its full XRT group
IDs. Images are hashed at admission and again at successful session exit; replays
use loaded BOs. A new ops/session instance is required to adopt edited source or
artifacts. This avoids reopening and hashing all sources at every operation.
The [28 passing opcode checks](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_single_image_checks_20261018_v3.log)
include A/B/C/A bit-identical replay and an extra completed operation followed by
deliberate modification of that probe's own cached manifest. Exit rejects the
changed identity, releases contexts, and restores the probe manifest. The
[structured report](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_single_image_checks_20261018_v3.json)
retains those checks and their criteria.

**MEASURED, checks-only observations:** the
[four selected complete synthetic cases](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_single_image_draft_20261018_v2.log)
pass unchanged numerical limits. The warm final E4B case uses 99 dispatches and
three context creations, with about 0.915 seconds total diagnostic wall time.
This includes image admission, validation, transport and host work. It is neither
a serving benchmark nor proof of hybrid benefit. The
[structured before/after record](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_single_image_draft_20261018.json)
retains the preceding version too, whose last-case wall time was about 5 seconds
despite only about 120 ms in dispatch waits. Avoiding repeated disk validation
removes much of that overhead. The broader 24-case numerical qualification remains
failed and is not superseded by these selected cases.

**MEASURED, real-input numerical qualification fails:** an external llama.cpp
evaluation-callback consumer captures the deployment Q5_K_M/PLE-Q4 targets on
ROCm0 using their pinned chat templates and a fixed public engineering prompt.
The prompt has 31 tokens. Its last normalized hidden state and prompt KV are
paired with the next target token's scaled embedding. The extra decode used to
obtain that embedding is kept separate; its advanced KV is not substituted.
The assistant interface converts these captured FP32 values once to BF16.
Original assistant BF16 weights then produce independent CPU reference fixtures.
Their shared KV source layers are 13/14 for E2B and 22/23 for E4B, with draft
position 31 and a 31-token shared cache.

The [bounded native draft check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_real_target_draft_20261018.log)
matches the reference greedy token in both cases but fails numerical limits in
both. E2B exceeds the maximum-error/reference-RMS bound after post-projection;
E4B exceeds limits in the last layer, final normalized state and post-projection.
Shared evaluated vocabulary logits remain within the recorded limits. No numerical
gate was changed. The [structured evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_real_target_draft_20261018.json)
retains target GGUF/DLL/source hashes, captured-tensor checksums, source-layer
mapping and per-stage errors. These are two offline draft steps on captured real
states, not target verification, acceptance measurement, agent evaluation or a
live hybrid chat assistant. Both device-cleanup witnesses pass; timing is ineligible.

### Matrix-unit projection, resident replay and target verification

The opcode dispatcher now supports the original matrix-unit BF16 projection as
well as compensated accumulation. Its program is 13,632 bytes, below the unchanged
16 KiB limit. The [bounded primitive check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_matrix_dispatch_checks_20261018.log)
passes all 28 reference/replay cases and the changed-manifest rejection; the
[structured report](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_matrix_dispatch_checks_20261018.json)
retains criteria and source identities. Stored operands/output remain BF16, with
FP32 accumulation. Neither choice guarantees every CPU-library rounding decision.

On the same real target states, [matrix-unit composition](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_matrix_real_draft_20261018.log)
passes the E2B numerical case but fails E4B; both greedy proposals match the CPU
reference. The [warm repeat](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_matrix_real_draft_warm_20261018.log)
reproduces that outcome. Its E2B/E4B wall observations are about 1.168/0.936 seconds,
including per-session admission and cleanup, with about 33.6/32.9 ms summed dispatch
waits. These are checks-only costs, not controlled serving latency. The
[structured record](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_matrix_real_draft_20261018.json)
preserves both attempts and all numerical limits unchanged.

A separate [resident-session check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_resident_replay_20261018.log)
alternates E2B/E4B/E2B/E4B under one session, with the same captured real states.
After both models' transactions are admitted, complete steps take about 150/152 ms
in the two diagnostic replays, including host packing and dispatch work but excluding
the later CPU reference comparisons and session-exit validation. Both replay every
saved native intermediate and output bit for bit, create no new contexts, and
release the owned context at exit. E4B's numerical failure remains. This hot replay
is not live chat throughput, a general context-length result, or hybrid speedup.
[Structured replay evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_resident_replay_20261018.json)
records the distinction.

**MEASURED, two offline one-step target checks:** the GPU capture consumer now
saves actual target logits after the prompt's bonus token. Before comparing those
logits to saved NPU proposals, every captured tensor must match the original input
capture bit for bit: 64 tensors for E2B, 100 for E4B. The
[verification record](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_target_verification_20261018.json)
checks target-logit hashes and greedy argmax, and finds both proposals equal the
target's next token (6719 and 563 respectively). Both correspond to the same fixed
31-token prompt, one step per model. This proves those two proposal comparisons;
it is not a general acceptance-rate estimate, a multi-token lossless verification
implementation, or permission to discard E4B's failed numerical gate.

The active assistant work now focuses on E2B at the user's request; E4B evidence
is retained for reference. An [E2B-only matrix-unit follow-up](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_matrix_full_20261018.log)
checks all twelve existing synthetic fixtures (three seeds, four cache lengths).
It passes eight numerical cases and matches eleven reference greedy tokens.
The [structured evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_matrix_full_20261018.json)
retains the four numerical failures and the token mismatch. The passing real-input
E2B case is therefore not promoted to broad numerical qualification. Realtime
serving, broader acceptance and agent evaluation remain open.

### E2B activation arena: two submitted streams (2026-10-18)

The generic BF16 command-stream builder now retains intermediate activations in
a 32 KiB tile-local arena. Its size-optimized dispatcher occupies 15,648 bytes
of the 16 KiB program limit; the existing stack/SRAM checks pass. The
[A/B/A device probe](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_state_checks_20261018_v2.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_state_checks_20261018_v2.json)) checks seven
outputs against the native packet baseline, all bitwise equal. This includes
odd-length softmax and chained GeGLU/residual activations. The host builder rejects
unwritten reads, out-of-bounds writes and overlapping projection input/output.
Inputs remain unchanged; device contexts are idle before and after.

The application composes the E2B body into 3,031 packets submitted together,
then gathers cluster-selected vocabulary rows on the host and submits a second
260-packet head stream. Thus one step needs two host submissions rather than
99 operation submissions. No activation arithmetic is substituted by CPU work.
The [first body check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_arena_real_20261018.log)
retains the initial three-submission version and context churn. The
[two-stream check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_arena_real_20261018_v2.log)
([registered inputs, builds and results](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_arena_real_20261018.json))
passes three repeats of the existing 31-token real ROCm fixture under the
unchanged full-step numerical gates. Preprojection, all four layer outputs,
final hidden/projected states, centroids, clusters, selected logits and token
match the existing matrix-unit NPU composition bit for bit. The token is 6719.
All submitted input BOs remain unchanged and owned contexts are released.

After compilation/admission, the last two diagnostic repeats take about 118 and
111 ms including host construction/copies, submission and readback, but excluding
later CPU reference comparisons and session-exit validation. Summed body/head
dispatch waits are about 30.9 and 30.7 ms. Both repeat streams hit the cached
program/BOs without creating contexts. The first repeat includes head compilation
and is not a warm observation. These checks-only observations are not controlled
serving timing, an independent acceptance sample or a demonstrated hybrid speedup.
The previously recorded four synthetic numerical failures remain unresolved;
this refactoring preserves the packet baseline's arithmetic and does not qualify
broader E2B accuracy. Live target-state transport, context-length coverage and
agent evaluation remain open. E4B stays outside the active implementation scope.

### Prepared E2B command templates (2026-10-18)

The [phase-instrumented E2B run](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_arena_profile_20261018.log)
([registered evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_arena_profile_20261018.json))
identifies roughly 40-50 ms per warm step in source hashing/build lookups,
plus body packet stacking and input/output transfers. The generic compiler
now snapshots sources once, caches checked build metadata, and prepares an
immutable body packet array before the replay loop. Session admission and exit
still verify source/artifact identities; full input BO readback/verification
still runs after every dispatch. No arithmetic or numerical criteria changed.

The [prepared input check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_prepared_checks_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_prepared_checks_20261018.json)) passes
seven native-operation outputs over A/B/A and three further prepared RMSNorm
executions with A/B/A input replacements. Unknown upload labels and changed
element counts are rejected before submission. The
[transport replay/drift check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_profile_transport_checks_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_profile_transport_checks_20261018.json))
passes all 28 existing cases, detects a changed admitted manifest, restores the
probe-owned file and releases contexts.

The [prepared E2B check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_prepared_real_20261018.log)
([registered evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_prepared_real_20261018.json))

native stage, selected logits and token over three repeats. The last two
diagnostic step observations are 62.46/62.21 ms. Body lookup/stacking has moved
out of those repeats; head construction remains inside. Summed body/head
dispatch waits are 30.39/30.27 ms. Each body input is about 49.9 MB, still fully
written and verified after submission. A separate embedding-server process was
active during the prepared and transport checks, recorded as foreign contention.
These are checks-only results, not a controlled before/after timing comparison.

This repeats one captured 31-token input and does not include changing target
KV, rotary factors or packet lengths. Prepared named uploads allow input-state
replacement with a template copy; general KV changes still require rebuilding
the corresponding packets. No live GPU/NPU serving throughput, real prompt
coverage, hybrid speedup or resolution of the four synthetic failures follows.

Prepared command streams now expose declared matrix and rotary-factor patches,

and rotary factors over A/B/A for both projection implementations. All six cases

bitwise, including a return to A without patches. Ten invalid matrix/rotary
updates are rejected. Inputs are unchanged and contexts are idle at exit.

A second real ROCm capture changes the public prompt from returning unique list
items to returning duplicate list items. Both prompts contain 31 tokens. The

in the registration. CPU BF16 references are regenerated from the captured

The B proposal is token 6719, equal to its captured GPU phase-1 logit argmax.
The original A fixture's source capture predates logit recording, so this run
records its direct GPU comparison as unavailable rather than borrowing B's
logits or the separate historical A verification. There is one new direct GPU
comparison, not three independent acceptance samples. The prompts are closely
related and both next tokens coincide; broader acceptance remains unmeasured.
An embedding-server job ran concurrently, so these checks carry no controlled
timing claim. This is fixed-length captured-state transport, not a live bridge,
incrementally growing conversation, broader numerical qualification or agent

### E2B growing-cache trajectory and RMSNorm diagnosis (2026-10-18)

The GPU capture consumer now supports 1-16 successive greedy decode steps under
one loaded target model/context. A five-step E2B capture has 192 tensors over
six phases and validated full-vocabulary logits for each phase. The independent
BF16 reference producer reconstructs each cache from prompt KV plus the
one-token deltas through phase p, pairs target hidden p with scaled embedding
p+1, and excludes phase p+1's advanced KV. Five reference states have cache
lengths/positions 31, 32, 33, 34 and 35. Each source delta, resulting length and
artifact hash is checked. The existing two-phase behavior remains available.

The [native trajectory check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_trajectory_20261018.log)
([registered evidence](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_trajectory_20261018.json))
builds separate templates for changed KV dimensions so projection padding and
softmax lengths agree, while reusing the compiler and exact program identities.
All exported native stages, clusters, logits and proposals match the existing
NPU packet composition bitwise at all five states and on return to the first
unpatched template. Four of five distinct states pass frozen numerical gates;
the 34-token state fails layer 3, hidden, postprojection and centroid criteria.
The extra first-state replay passes and is not a sixth independent state.
Inputs remain unchanged and all contexts are released. The five one-step
proposals are 6719, 107, 2063, 18853, 1419; GPU greedy verification gives
6719, 107, 2543, 28751, 1419. This is three matching teacher-forced proposals
on one short public prompt, not multi-token chain acceptance or lossless serving.

A [standalone reproduction](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_trajectory_failure_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_trajectory_failure_20261018.json))
retains the 34-token failure and complete native traces. CPU diagnostics
recompute each operation from its actual NPU input. The first local mismatch is
five values in layer 1 query RMSNorm; other checked local operations are exact
on their actual inputs. The [rounding diagnostic](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_norm_rounding_20261018.json)
reproduces these five values using four FP32 Newton iterations. On the first
query row, that inverse square root is one FP32 ULP below torch's result.
A compensated residual removes those differences in the CPU diagnostic.

The first separate NPU correction, using `aie::msc`, produces a
[bit-identical failed trace](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_refined_norm_failure_case_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_refined_norm_failure_case_20261018.json)).
It does not validate the CPU diagnostic's fused residual assumption. A second
[product-split attempt](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_refined_norm_split_20261018.log)
fails to compile with a vector G_AND legalization error. Replacing that mask
with explicit shifts [compiles](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_refined_norm_split_build_20261018.log)
to 6,432 bytes with a 1,408-byte stack frame. Its
[isolated norm check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_refined_norm_split_checks_20261018.log)
passes all 546 cases: 21 norms, two poison values, twelve synthetic E2B states
and the failing real state. The original norm kernel and arena path remain the
control; isolated one-ULP correctness is not full-model adoption. These runs
are checks-only; several observed concurrent embedding-server work.

The [complete split-correction check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_refined_norm_full_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_refined_norm_full_20261018.json))
retains all seventeen cases. It passes nine of twelve synthetic E2B states
(previous matrix-unit control: eight) and four of five real trajectory states.
All seventeen greedy tokens match the CPU assistant reference. The 34-token
failure remains and its saved native trace is bit-identical to the control.
The isolated pass therefore does not repair the identified real full-step
failure. The variance and inverse bits in the CPU diagnosis are CPU values,
not directly observed NPU variance registers; the exact source of the residual
rounding discrepancy still needs device evidence. No change to the original
kernel, frozen tolerances or serving default is justified by these results.

At the user's request, subsequent hardware work starts with the read-only
`tools/check-inference-contention.ps1` preflight: sampled CPU inference work,

monitoring after admission. The first check detects the existing CPU embedding

### Device-observed normalization products and BF16-aware correction (2026-10-18)

The [state probe](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_norm_state_probe_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_norm_state_probe_20261018.json)) reads
actual FP32 variance and inverse bits from the NPU norm kernel on the saved
34-token layer-1 query input. Variance differs from torch in heads 0 and 3;
head 0's inverse already matches torch. These observations supersede the
earlier CPU-only inference that the inverse correction alone could fix the
five BF16 differences. A changed inverse calculation is insufficient here.

The [product probe](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_norm_products_probe_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_norm_products_probe_20261018.json)) also
exports element 129's FP32 products. In head 0 the first product matches an
IEEE FP32 CPU multiplication using the actual NPU inverse. The last product's
bits are 3188621312 on the device versus 3188621313 for the CPU product using
the actual NPU intermediate. That one-ULP difference crosses a BF16 rounding
boundary. The complete normalized output still matches the saved failing trace,
so this is evidence from the actual discrepancy, not an unrelated input.

A separate `exact_norm=True` candidate computes the two normalization products
with integer significands, exploiting that one operand is exactly BF16. A
[diagnostic check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_norm_exact_cpu_check_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_norm_exact_cpu_check_20261018.json))
then finds zero BF16 differences from the CPU norm result on that input. The
[standalone build](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_norm_build_20261018.log)
and [546 norm cases](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_norm_checks_20261018.log)
pass the original isolated one-ULP/relative-error limits.

The [first wider product sweep](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_product_bitwise_checks_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_product_bitwise_checks_20261018.json))
retains two failures at signed smallest-normal values multiplied by the FP32
value immediately below one: the correctly rounded result is normal, but the
initial helper delegates the pre-rounding underflow case to the control, which
returns zero. An integer boundary correction resolves them. The
[updated sweep](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_product_bitwise_checks_20261018_v2.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_product_bitwise_checks_20261018_v2.json))
passes all 243,581 eligible products bitwise. It covers every normal finite
BF16 encoding at three fixed FP32 scales plus seeded random pairs with normal
finite operands and results. It does not qualify the remaining exceptional or
subnormal fallback paths or exhaust every FP32 right operand.

The [initial complete norm candidate](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_exact_norm_full_20261018.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_exact_norm_full_20261018.json)) and
[post-boundary-fix check](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_exact_norm_full_20261018_v2.log)
([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_e2b_exact_norm_full_20261018_v2.json)) both
pass fourteen of seventeen full-model numerical cases: nine of twelve synthetic
states and all five real trajectory states, including the previous 34-token

This does not change the earlier three-of-five comparison with GPU target
tokens; CPU-assistant agreement is a different property. The three synthetic
failures remain recorded and the original norm and arena dispatcher stay the
default. The final standalone exact-product norm occupies 7,840 bytes with a
1,920-byte stack frame; bounds pass. It runs through a separate image and is

Every device run above follows the requested contention preflight. The full

### Corrected normalization inside the E2B arena (2026-10-18)

`ArenaCompiler(exact_norm=True)` now selects a distinct matrix-only program
with the BF16-aware normalization products. The original compiler remains the
default and still supports both projection implementations. The experimental
compiler rejects compensated projection requests before packet construction;
it does not silently change opcode 1's arithmetic to matrix-unit arithmetic.
Build identity includes the mode, optimization and all relevant headers.

The [first combined build](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_arena_build_20261018.log)
has 18,288 bytes of code and is rejected by the 16 KiB program limit. Sharing
the product helpers [reduces it](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_arena_build_20261018_v2.log)
to 17,360 bytes, still rejected. `-Oz`
[fits code](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_arena_build_20261018_v3.log)
at 12,880 bytes but fails the conservative stack sum plus margin. Selectively
inlining BF16 widening/rounding helpers while keeping larger arithmetic helpers
shared produces the [passing build](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_arena_build_20261018_v4.log):
12,144 code bytes and 3,424 bytes of summed stack frames plus the existing
256-byte margin, within the unchanged 4 KiB reserve. SRAM placement checks also
pass. Failed builds are retained; none ran on hardware.

state. Every checked preprojection, layer output, hidden/projected state,
centroid vector, selected cluster/row logits and token matches the standalone
corrected NPU composition bitwise. The frozen CPU numerical gates pass at all
five distinct states. Body and clustered head need two submissions and share
one exact PDI/interface context without eviction across the whole replay;

GPU-token comparison is unchanged; assistant-reference agreement does not

([JSON](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_control_arena_regression_20261018.json))

The model run starts with an [idle preflight](../results/aie/transformer_bf16_exact_arena_preflight_20261018.json),
